--- generic-subclass-construction @gencs
// Review focus 4: generic subclasses after erasure, each built through gencs's __hx_ctor__G<T_c> helper
// with its own type arguments (G<object>.__hx_ctor__G<U_c>, <int>, <object>), field initializers included.
// Overrides in a subclass of an erased instantiation take the base's CLR slot (SubC's `object get()`,
// `set(object __temp_x1)`), as gencs's FixOverrides gives them, and so does a BalancedTree compare.
class C {
	public var n:Int;
	public function new(n:Int) this.n = n;
	public function toString() return "C" + n;
}
class G<T> {
	public var v:T;
	public var count:Int = 7;
	public var tag:String = "g";
	public var seen:Array<T> = [];
	public function new(v:T) {
		this.v = v;
		seen.push(v);
	}
	public function get():T return v;
	public function set(x:T):Void v = x;
}
class Sub<U> extends G<U> {
	public var extra:Array<U> = [];
	public var k:Int = 11;
	public function new(u:U) {
		super(u);
		extra.push(u);
	}
	override public function get():U return extra[0];
	override public function set(x:U):Void {
		extra.push(x);
		super.set(x);
	}
}
class SubI extends G<Int> {
	public var z:Int = 3;
	public function new(x:Int) super(x + 1);
	override public function get():Int return v * 100;
	override public function set(x:Int):Void v = x + 1000;
}
class SubC extends G<C> {
	public var w:String = "w";
	public function new(c:C) super(c);
	override public function get():C return new C(v.n * 10);
	override public function set(x:C):Void v = new C(x.n + 100);
}
class Key {
	public var id:Int;
	public function new(id:Int) this.id = id;
	public function toString() return "K" + id;
}
class KeyTree extends haxe.ds.BalancedTree<Key, String> {
	public function new() super();
	override function compare(k1:Key, k2:Key):Int return k1.id - k2.id;
}
class P {
	static function show(label:String, x:Dynamic) {
		var c = Type.getClass(x);
		Sys.println(label + ": " + Std.string(c) + " super " + Std.string(Type.getSuperClass(c)));
	}
	static function main() {
		var g = new G<C>(new C(1));
		show("G<C>", g);
		Sys.println(g.v + " " + g.count + " " + g.tag + " " + g.seen);
		var sc = new Sub<C>(new C(2));
		show("Sub<C>", sc);
		Sys.println(sc.v + " " + sc.count + " " + sc.tag + " " + sc.seen + " " + sc.extra + " " + sc.k);
		var si = new Sub<Int>(5);
		show("Sub<Int>", si);
		Sys.println(si.v + " " + si.count + " " + si.tag + " " + si.seen + " " + si.extra + " " + si.k);
		var sn = new Sub<Null<Int>>(null);
		show("Sub<Null<Int>>", sn);
		Sys.println(sn.v + " " + sn.count + " " + sn.seen + " " + sn.extra);
		var ss = new Sub<String>("s");
		show("Sub<String>", ss);
		Sys.println(ss.v + " " + ss.seen + " " + ss.extra);
		var i = new SubI(4);
		show("SubI", i);
		Sys.println(i.v + " " + i.count + " " + i.tag + " " + i.seen + " " + i.z);
		var c = new SubC(new C(3));
		show("SubC", c);
		Sys.println(c.v + " " + c.count + " " + c.tag + " " + c.seen + " " + c.w + " " + c.v.n);
		var gi:G<Int> = i;
		var gc:G<C> = c;
		Sys.println(gi.v + " " + gc.v.n);
		// Overrides, called directly, through the base instantiation and through Dynamic.
		Sys.println(gc.get().n + " " + c.get().n);
		gc.set(new C(1));
		Sys.println(c.v.n + " " + gc.get().n);
		var dc:Dynamic = c;
		dc.set(new C(2));
		Sys.println(dc.get().n + " " + c.v.n);
		Sys.println(gi.get() + " " + i.get());
		gi.set(6);
		Sys.println(i.v + " " + gi.get());

// Shapes left refused. A generic interface's Null<T> instantiated with String is a haxe.lang.Null<string>
// in its CLR signature, which a String implementation cannot reach (gencs's C# fails with CS0535 and
// CS0738). An override of an @:overload'ed method of G<C> that changes only the return type takes the
// slot with C#'s covariant return in gencs, which hxc does not write.
class C { public function new() {} }
interface I<T> { function f(x:Null<T>):Int; }
class CS implements I<String> {
	public function new() {}
	public function f(x:Null<String>):Int return x == null ? 0 : x.length;
}
interface J<T> { function g():Null<T>; }
class CJ implements J<String> {
	public function new() {}
	public function g():Null<String> return "j";
}
class G<T> {
	public function new() {}
	@:overload public function g(x:Int):T return null;
	@:overload public function g(x:String):String return "G.g(String)";
}
class S extends G<C> {
	public function new() super();
	@:overload override public function g(x:Int):C return new C();
}
class P {
	static function main() {
		var i:I<String> = new CS();
		Sys.println(i.f("abc"));
		var j:J<String> = new CJ();
		Sys.println(j.g());
		Sys.println(new S().g(1));
	}
}

		try Sys.println(n + " " + f()) catch (e:Dynamic) Sys.println(n + " EXC " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e)));

--- abstract-impl-type-parameters @gencs
// An abstract's constructor and member methods are its implementation's statics, generic over their
// own type parameters and then the abstract's, Pr_Impl_.then<R,T>(Th<T> this1, …): a call binds the
// abstract's T from the receiver, as gencs's then<object,int>((Th<int>) listInts()), the implicit
// @:to cast's toArr<int> too. Ds is shaped like haxeui's DataSource: a generic @:from static and a
// function-typed T (each<object>). A generic @:from or @:op static whose T Haxe leaves unbound is
// fromValue<object>, of<object> and cat<object>, as in gencs: its arguments and result go through
// __hx_cast (Bag, over a class). Over an interface (Ds, TBag) gencs's parent cast returns `this`, so the
// __hx_cast<string> of fromValue's Th<object> throws InvalidCastException; hxc's copies (decision 2 of
// plan 3c), a recorded divergence, so [run] is hxc's output and [gencs] gencs's.
interface Th<T> { function then<R>(f:T->R):Th<R>; }
class FP<T> implements Th<T> {
	var v:T;
	public function new(v:T) this.v = v;
	public function then<R>(f:T->R):Th<R> return new FP<R>(f(v));
}
abstract Pr<T>(Th<T>) from Th<T> to Th<T> {
	public function then<R>(f:T->R):Pr<R> return this.then(f);
}
abstract Ds<T>(Th<T>) from Th<T> {
	@:from static function fromValue<T>(v:T):Ds<T> return new FP(v);
	public function each(f:T->Void):Void this.then(x -> { f(x); return null; });
}
abstract Bx<T>(Th<T>) {
	public function new(x:Th<T>) this = x;
	public function wrap():Array<T> return [];
	@:to public function toArr():Array<T> return [];
	@:op(A + B) public function add(o:Bx<T>):Bx<T> return new Bx(this);
	public function later():Void->Array<T> return () -> new Array<T>();
	public function count():Int return wrap().length + 1;
}
abstract Bag<T>(FP<T>) from FP<T> to FP<T> {
	@:op(A + B) static function cat<T>(a:Bag<T>, b:Bag<T>):Bag<T> return new FP(a.get());
	@:from static function of<T>(v:T):Bag<T> return new FP(v);
	public function get():T return @:privateAccess this.v;
}
abstract TBag<T>(Th<T>) from Th<T> to Th<T> {
	@:op(A + B) static function cat<T>(a:TBag<T>, b:TBag<T>):TBag<T> return a;
}
class Folder { public var id:String; public function new(id) this.id = id; }
class P {
	static function listFolders():Pr<Array<Folder>> return new FP([new Folder("a")]);
	static function listInts():Pr<Int> return new FP(1);
	static function main() {
		listInts().then(x -> { Sys.println(x); return null; });
		listFolders().then(l -> { Sys.println(l[0].id); return null; });
		listFolders().then(l -> { Sys.println(l.length); return 1; });
		var d:Ds<Int->Int> = (x -> x + 1);
		d.each(g -> Sys.println(g(2)));
		var b = new Bx(new FP(1));
		Sys.println(Type.getClass(b.wrap()));
		var a:Array<Int> = b;
		Sys.println(Type.getClass(a));
		Sys.println(Type.getClass((b + b).wrap()));
		Sys.println(Type.getClass(b.later()()));
		Sys.println(b.count());
		var bs = new Bx(new FP("s"));
		Sys.println(Type.getClass(bs.wrap()));
		var b1:Bag<Int> = 4;
		Sys.println(b1.get() + 1);
		var b2:Bag<Int> = new FP(6);
		var b3 = b1 + b2;
		Sys.println(b3.get() + " " + Type.getClass((b3 : FP<Int>)));
		try {
			var ds:Ds<String> = "x";
			ds.each(s -> Sys.println(s));
		} catch (e:Dynamic) Sys.println("Ds<String> threw " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e)));
		try {
			var t1:TBag<Int> = new FP(7);
			var t3 = t1 + t1;
			Sys.println(Type.getClass((t3 : Th<Int>)));
		} catch (e:Dynamic) Sys.println("TBag threw " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e)));
	}
}

// Which members a companion interface declares: every kept non-static, non-dynamic method the class itself
// declares whose Haxe signature mentions no type parameter (types notes §3), read through
// Type.getInstanceFields and through .NET reflection over the companions G and GS.
import cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags;

class G<T> {
	public var v:T;
	public var n:Int = 1;
	public function new(v:T) this.v = v;
	public function a():Int return 1;
	function priv():String return "p";
	public function withC(c:G<C>):Array<C> return [];
	public function withDyn(d:G<Dynamic>):Void {}
	public function nullT(x:Null<T>):Void {}
	public function arrT(x:Array<T>):Void {}
	public function fnT(f:T->Void):Void {}
	public function fnPlain(f:Int->Void):Void {}
	public function gen<U>(u:U):Int return 0;
	public function genNoU<U>():Int return 0;
	public static function stat():Int return 0;
	public dynamic function dyn():Int return 0;
	public inline function inl():Int return 0;
	public function ov(x:Int):Int return x;
	public function toString():String return "G";
	@:keep public function kept():Int return 2;
	public var prop(get, never):Int;
	function get_prop() return 3;
	public function anon():{a:Int} return {a: 1};
	public function optInt(?x:Int):Void {}
	public function defInt(x:Int = 3):Void {}
}

	public function new(u:U) super(u);
	override public function a():Int return 2;
	public function own():Int return 3;

class P {
	static function typeName(t:cs.system.Type):String return t == null ? "null" : t.ToString();
	static function dumpType(label:String, t:cs.system.Type) {
		if (t == null) {
			Sys.println(label + ": not found");
			return;
		}
		var ifs = [for (i in t.GetInterfaces()) typeName(i)];
		ifs.sort(Reflect.compare);
		Sys.println(label + ": " + typeName(t) + (t.IsInterface ? " interface" : "") + " implements " + ifs.join(","));
		var attrs = t.GetCustomAttributes(false);
		for (i in 0...attrs.Length) {
			var g = cs.Lib.as(attrs[i], cs.internal.HxObject.GenericInterface);
			if (g != null) Sys.println("  [GenericInterface(" + typeName(g.generic) + ")]");
		}
		var flags = new cs.Flags(BindingFlags.Public) | BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly;
		var ms = t.GetMethods(flags);
		for (i in 0...ms.Length) {
			var n = ms[i].Name;
			if (StringTools.startsWith(n, "__hx_") && n != "__hx_cast") continue;
			Sys.println("  " + Std.string(ms[i]) + (ms[i].IsStatic ? " static" : ""));
		}
	}
	static function main() {
		var g = new G<Int>(1);
		g.a(); g.withC(null); g.withDyn(null); g.nullT(null); g.arrT(null); g.fnT(null); g.fnPlain(null); g.gen(1); g.genNoU(); G.stat(); g.dyn(); g.inl(); g.ov(1); g.toString(); g.prop; g.anon(); g.optInt(); g.defInt();
		var s = new GS<Int>(1); s.own();
		Sys.println(Type.getInstanceFields(G));
		Sys.println(Type.getInstanceFields(GS));
		dumpType("G companion", cs.system.Type._GetType("G"));
		dumpType("GS companion", cs.system.Type._GetType("GS"));
	}

--- cast-member-order @gencs
// Order of the X_cast members a generic class gets from its superclass and its generic interfaces (deep),
// read with Type.getInstanceFields (types notes §3, probes castorder and ifacecast).
interface I1<T> { function a():T; }
interface I2<A, B> { function b(x:A):B; }
interface I3<T> extends I1<T> { function c():T; }
interface IExt<T> extends I1<T> { function c():T; }
class Base<T> implements I1<T> { public function new() {} public function a():T return null; }
class X<T> extends Base<T> implements I2<T, T> implements I3<T> {
	public function new() super();
	public function b(x:T):T return x;
	public function c():T return null;
}
class Y<T> extends X<T> { public function new() super(); }
final class Fin<T> implements I1<T> { public function new() {} public function a():T return null; }
class Perm<X, Y> implements I2<Y, X> {
	public function new() {}
	public function b(x:Y):X return null;
}
class Fixed<T> implements I1<Int> {
	public var t:T;
	public function new() {}
	public function a():Int return 1;
}
class Nested<T> implements I1<Array<T>> {
	public function new() {}
	public function a():Array<T> return [];
}
class Partial<T> implements I2<String, T> {
	public function new() {}
	public function b(x:String):T return null;
}
class Both<T> implements I1<T> implements I2<T, T> {
	public function new() {}
	public function a():T return null;
	public function b(x:T):T return x;
}
class Derived<U> extends Base<U> {
	public function new() super();
}
class DerivedFixed extends Base<String> {
	public function new() super();
}
class Derived2<A, B> extends Base<B> {
	public function new() super();
}
class ImplExt<T> implements IExt<T> {
	public function new() {}
	public function a():T return null;
	public function c():T return null;
}
class P {
	static function main() {
		Sys.println(Type.getInstanceFields(X));
		Sys.println(Type.getInstanceFields(Y));
		Sys.println(Type.getInstanceFields(Fin));
		var all:Array<Dynamic> = [new Perm<Int, String>(), new Fixed<String>(), new Nested<Int>(), new Partial<Int>(), new Both<Int>(), new Derived<Int>(), new DerivedFixed(), new Derived2<Int, String>(), new ImplExt<Int>()];
		for (x in all) Sys.println(Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(x)) + ": " + Type.getInstanceFields(Type.getClass(x)));
	}
}

--- cast-bodies @gencs
// The bodies of the cast members, called through .NET reflection (no Haxe code calls them before the
// casts' call sites). A class that is not generic implementing a generic interface returns itself from
// IG_cast. An X_cast copy converts each element of a NativeArray<Array<T>> field through Array's __hx_cast,
// a null element staying null. A superclass's NativeArray field whose element is no longer a type parameter
// (Sub<U> extends Base<Int>) is still copied element by element, by the field's declared type, as gencs does,
// so the copy does not share it. A generic subclass of an abstract generic class has an X_cast of its own,
// which copies its fields.
interface IG<T> { function ig():T; function igPlain():Int; }
class NI implements IG<String> {
	public function new() {}
	public function ig():String return "ni";
	public function igPlain():Int return 3;
}
class G<T> {
	public var v:T;
	public var aa:cs.NativeArray<Array<T>>;
	public function new(v:T) this.v = v;
}
class Base<T> {
	public var na:cs.NativeArray<T>;
	public function new() {}
}
class Sub<U> extends Base<Int> {
	public function new() super();
}
abstract class Ab<T> {
	public function new() {}
	public abstract function f():T;
}
class AbI<T> extends Ab<T> {
	public var t:T;
	public function new(t:T) {
		super();
		this.t = t;
	}
	public function f():T return t;
}
class P {
	static function callCast(o:Dynamic, name:String, args:Array<cs.system.Type>):Dynamic {
		var m = cs.Lib.getNativeType(o).GetMethod(name);
		var na = new cs.NativeArray<cs.system.Type>(args.length);
		for (i in 0...args.length) na[i] = args[i];
		return m.MakeGenericMethod(na).Invoke(o, null);
	}
	static function main() {
		var tInt = cs.Lib.getNativeType(1), tFloat = cs.Lib.getNativeType(1.5), tStr = cs.Lib.toNativeType(String);
		var ni = new NI();
		Sys.println("NI: " + Type.getInstanceFields(NI));
		Sys.println("NI IG_cast is this: " + (callCast(ni, "IG_cast", [tInt]) == ni));
		var g = new G<Int>(5);
		g.aa = cs.NativeArray.make([3, 4], null);
		var gd:Dynamic = callCast(g, "G_cast", [tFloat]);
		var gf:G<Float> = gd;
		var oldAa:Dynamic = g.aa, newAa:Dynamic = gf.aa;
		Sys.println("G<Float>: v=" + gf.v + " aa.Length=" + gf.aa.Length + " aa[0]=" + gf.aa[0] + " aa[1]=" + gf.aa[1] + " copied=" + (newAa != oldAa));
		var s = new Sub<Int>();
		s.na = cs.NativeArray.make(1, 2);
		var sd:Dynamic = callCast(s, "Sub_cast", [tStr]);
		var ss:Sub<String> = sd;
		var oldNa:Dynamic = s.na, newNa:Dynamic = ss.na;
		Sys.println("Sub<String>: copy=" + (sd != (s : Dynamic)) + " na[1]=" + ss.na[1] + " shared=" + (newNa == oldNa));
		var ab = new AbI<Dynamic>(3);
		var abd:Dynamic = callCast(ab, "AbI_cast", [tInt]);
		var abi:AbI<Int> = abd;
		Sys.println("AbI AbI_cast: copy=" + (abd != (ab : Dynamic)) + " t=" + abi.t + " f=" + abi.f());
		Sys.println("AbI: " + Type.getInstanceFields(AbI));
	}
}

--- struct-and-abstract-base-casts
// Casts gencs has no working body for, called through .NET reflection. A @:struct implementing a generic
// interface returns itself boxed (gencs's C# for a generic struct doesn't compile; spec, Casts between
// generic instantiations). A class that is not generic inherits its abstract generic base's own cast,
// whose gencs body calls itself until the stack overflows; hxc returns `this` for the class's own type
// arguments and throws InvalidCastException for others (decision 4 of plan 3c). A generic subclass's parent
// cast converts (decision 2), where gencs's returns the object unchanged.
interface IG<T> { function ig():T; }
@:struct class S implements IG<String> {
	public var x:Int;
	public function new(x:Int) this.x = x;
	public function ig():String return "s" + x;
}
@:struct class GS<T> implements IG<T> {
	public var t:T;
	public function new(t:T) this.t = t;
	public function ig():T return t;
}
abstract class Ab<T> {
	public function new() {}
	public abstract function f():T;
}
class Concrete extends Ab<Int> {
	public function new() super();
	public function f():Int return 1;
}
class AbI<T> extends Ab<T> {
	public var t:T;
	public function new(t:T) {
		super();
		this.t = t;
	}
	public function f():T return t;
}
class P {
	static function callCast(o:Dynamic, name:String, args:Array<cs.system.Type>):Dynamic {
		var m = cs.Lib.getNativeType(o).GetMethod(name);
		var na = new cs.NativeArray<cs.system.Type>(args.length);
		for (i in 0...args.length) na[i] = args[i];
		return m.MakeGenericMethod(na).Invoke(o, null);
	}
	static function main() {
		var tInt = cs.Lib.getNativeType(1), tStr = cs.Lib.toNativeType(String);
		var s:IG<String> = new S(4);
		var back:IG<String> = callCast(s, "IG_cast", [tStr]);
		Sys.println("S IG_cast: " + back.ig() + " " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(back)));
		var gs:IG<Int> = new GS<Int>(7);
		var gback:IG<Int> = callCast(gs, "IG_cast", [tInt]);
		Sys.println("GS IG_cast: " + gback.ig());
		var c = new Concrete();
		Sys.println("Concrete Ab_cast<Int> is this: " + (callCast(c, "Ab_cast", [tInt]) == c));
		try {
			callCast(c, "Ab_cast", [tStr]);
			Sys.println("Concrete Ab_cast<String>: no exception");
		} catch (e:cs.system.reflection.TargetInvocationException) {
			Sys.println("Concrete Ab_cast<String>: " + e.InnerException.GetType().ToString());
		}
		var ab:Dynamic = new AbI<Dynamic>(3);
		var abd:Dynamic = callCast(ab, "Ab_cast", [tInt]);
		var abi:AbI<Int> = abd;
		Sys.println("AbI Ab_cast<Int>: copy=" + (abd != ab) + " t=" + abi.t);
	}
}

# Casts notes §6.1, merged with types notes §8.16's map-abstract-downcast (probe mapdowncast: an enum-keyed
# local, a static with an initializer, Map<String,Array<String>>, Map<Int,C>, and a write through a typed

--- cast-map-member @gencs
// Member access on a Map<K,V> static, local or anonymous field: Haxe's @:multiType abstract casts `this`
// (IMap<K,V>) to its specialization (StringMap<V>, IntMap<V>, ObjectMap<K,V>, EnumValueMap<K,V>) with the same
// type arguments. gencs writes __hx_cast, which returns the object itself (casts notes fact 6, types notes §0.8).
// The last line: a write through a typed anonymous field read reaches the original map (an identity cast).
enum E {
	A;
	B(i:Int);
}

class K {
	public var x = 1;
	public function new() {}
}

class P {
	static var em:Map<E, Bool> = new Map();
	static var sm:Map<String, Int> = new Map();
	static var im:Map<Int, String> = new Map();
	static var om:Map<K, Float> = new Map();
	static var dm:Map<String, Dynamic> = new Map();
	static var anon:{m:Map<String, Int>} = {m: new Map()};
	static var tz:Map<E, Array<String>> = [A => ["x"]];

	static function main() {
		em.set(A, true);
		em[B(1)] = false;
		Sys.println(em.get(A) + " " + em.exists(B(2)) + " " + em[B(1)]);
		sm["a"] = 1;
		sm.set("b", 2);
		Sys.println(sm["a"] + sm.get("b"));
		im.set(1, "x");
		Sys.println(im.get(1) + " " + im.remove(1) + " " + im.exists(1));
		var k = new K();
		om.set(k, 1.5);
		Sys.println(om.get(k));
		dm.set("q", 1.5);
		Sys.println(dm.get("q"));
		anon.m.set("z", 26);
		Sys.println(anon.m.get("z"));
		var keys = [for (key in sm.keys()) key];
		keys.sort(Reflect.compare);
		Sys.println(keys);
		var total = 0;
		for (key => v in sm) total += v;
		for (v in sm) total += v;
		Sys.println(total);
		for (key => v in em) Sys.println(Std.string(key) + "=" + v);
		var m:Map<E, Bool> = new Map();
		m.set(A, true);
		Sys.println(m.exists(A) + " " + m.get(A) + " " + m.exists(B(1)));
		var ms:Map<String, Array<String>> = new Map();
		ms.set("k", ["v"]);
		Sys.println(ms.exists("k") + " " + ms.get("k"));
		var mi:Map<Int, K> = new Map();
		mi.set(1, new K());
		Sys.println(mi.get(1).x);
		Sys.println(tz.exists(A) ? tz[A].length : -1);
		var d:Dynamic = {prefs: m};
		var typed:{prefs:Map<E, Bool>} = d;
		typed.prefs.set(B(1), false);
		Sys.println(m.exists(B(1)));
	}
}

# Casts notes §6.6: gencs's __hx_cast copy, including the map copy that corrupts the original and the lost
# List add (casts fact 9, kept as gencs bugs the spec reproduces). Two-key StringMaps are printed sorted and the
# serialization of the original is searched, because String.GetHashCode is randomized per process.
--- cast-generic-copy @gencs
// A Dynamic holding X<Dynamic> cast to X<Int>: gencs's __hx_cast builds a new object and copies every field,
// converting native arrays of T with genericCast and casting generic-typed fields again through setField.
// Maps share their keys/hashes arrays with the copy, so a write through the copy shows its key in the
// original with a null value; a List copy loses adds. hxcs bugs, reproduced. @gencs.
// A StringMap's key order follows String.GetHashCode, which .NET randomizes per process, so two-key StringMaps
// are printed with their entries sorted (srt) and the original's serialization is only searched for `y1:qn`.
import haxe.ds.*;

enum E {
	A;
	B(x:Int);
}

class Box<T> {
	public var v:T;
	public var n:Int;

	public function new(v:T) {
		this.v = v;
		n = 7;
	}
}

class P {
	static function run(name:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try {
			Sys.println(name + ": " + Std.string(f()));
		} catch (e:Dynamic) {
			var s = Std.string(e);
			if (s.length > 100) s = s.substr(0, 100);
			Sys.println(name + ": EXC " + s.split("\n")[0].split("\r")[0]);
		}
	}

	static function srt(s:String):String {
		var parts = s.substr(1, s.length - 2).split(", ");
		parts.sort(Reflect.compare);
		return "[" + parts.join(", ") + "]";
	}

	static function takeIntMap(m:StringMap<Int>)
		m.set("y", 5);

	static function main() {
		run("StringMap", () -> { var m = new StringMap<Dynamic>(); m.set("a", 1.5); var d:Dynamic = m; var t:StringMap<Int> = d; t.set("q", 3); srt(m.toString()) + " " + srt(t.toString()) + " " + (m.get("q") == null) + " " + (haxe.Serializer.run(m).indexOf("y1:qn") >= 0); });
		run("StringMap same", () -> { var m = new StringMap<Int>(); var d:Dynamic = m; var t:StringMap<Int> = d; t.set("q", 3); m.toString() + " " + (t == m); });
		run("StringMap arg cast", () -> { var m = new StringMap<Dynamic>(); m.set("a", 1); takeIntMap(cast m); srt(m.toString()); });
		run("StringMap bad", () -> { var m = new StringMap<Dynamic>(); m.set("a", 1); var d:Dynamic = m; var t:StringMap<String> = d; t.toString(); });
		run("IntMap", () -> { var m = new IntMap<Dynamic>(); m.set(1, 1); var d:Dynamic = m; var t:IntMap<Float> = d; t.set(2, 2.5); m.toString() + " " + t.toString(); });
		run("ObjectMap", () -> { var m = new ObjectMap<Dynamic, Dynamic>(); var k = {}; m.set(k, 1); var d:Dynamic = m; var t:ObjectMap<Dynamic, Int> = d; t.get(k); });
		run("EnumValueMap", () -> { var m = new EnumValueMap<E, Dynamic>(); m.set(A, 1); var d:Dynamic = m; var t:EnumValueMap<E, Int> = d; t.set(B(1), 2); m.toString() + " " + t.toString(); });
		run("BalancedTree", () -> { var m = new BalancedTree<String, Dynamic>(); m.set("a", 1); var d:Dynamic = m; var t:BalancedTree<String, Int> = d; t.set("b", 2); m.toString() + " " + t.toString(); });
		run("List", () -> { var l = new List<Dynamic>(); l.add(1); var d:Dynamic = l; var t:List<Int> = d; t.add(2); l.toString() + " " + t.toString() + " " + t.length; });
		run("List bad", () -> { var l = new List<Dynamic>(); l.add(1); var d:Dynamic = l; var t:List<String> = d; t.toString(); });
		run("Box", () -> { var b = new Box<Dynamic>(2.5); var d:Dynamic = b; var t:Box<Int> = d; t.v = 4; b.v + " " + t.v + " " + t.n + " " + Std.string(Type.typeof(t)); });
		run("Box bad", () -> { var b = new Box<Dynamic>(3); var d:Dynamic = b; var t:Box<String> = d; t.v; });
		run("Box typed cast", () -> { var b = new Box<Int>(3); var t:Box<Float> = cast b; t.v = 2.5; b.v; });
		run("Box setField", () -> { var h = new Holder(); var b = new Box<Dynamic>(1.5); Reflect.setField(h, "b", b); h.b.v = 9; b.v + " " + h.b.v; });
	}
}

class Holder {
	public var b:Box<Int>;

	public function new() {}
}

# Casts notes §6.7 minus the three FP -> Th casts and `IMap from Dynamic`, which work in hxc

--- cast-interface @gencs
// Casts into an instantiation of a generic interface. gencs's Th_cast<T_c> implementation passes the class's
// own T (and IMap gets no __hx_cast at all), so a mismatched instantiation always ends in an
// InvalidCastException: an anonymous field typed Map<String,Int> holding an unserialized StringMap throws on
// every access. @gencs.
// The FP<Dynamic> -> Th<Int>, Th<Int> -> Th<Float> and Dynamic -> IMap<String,Int> casts are in
// interface-cast-fixed: hxc fixes gencs's parent-cast bodies (FP.Th_cast, StringMap.haxe_IMap_cast), so they
// work instead of throwing. The anonymous Map<String,Int> field is a plain castclass to IMap<string,int> in
// gencs (no __hx_cast), so it throws in both.
interface Th<T> {
	function get():T;
}

class FP<T> implements Th<T> {
	var v:T;

	public function new(v:T)
		this.v = v;

	public function get():T
		return v;
}

typedef TM = {m:Map<String, Int>};
typedef TO = {m:Map<String, FP<Int>>};

class P {
	static function run(name:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try {
			Sys.println(name + ": " + Std.string(f()));
		} catch (e:Dynamic) {
			var s = Std.string(e);
			if (s.length > 100) s = s.substr(0, 100);
			Sys.println(name + ": EXC " + s.split("\n")[0].split("\r")[0]);
		}
	}

	static function main() {
		run("Dynamic(FP<Int>) -> Th<Int>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new FP<Int>(1); var x:Th<Int> = d; x.get(); });
		run("Dynamic(FP<Dyn>) -> FP<Int>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new FP<Dynamic>(1); var x:FP<Int> = d; x.get(); });
		run("FP<Int> -> Th<Dynamic>", () -> { var x:Th<Dynamic> = new FP<Int>(1); x.get(); });
		run("anon Map<String,Int> unserialized", () -> { var t:TM = haxe.Unserializer.run(haxe.Serializer.run({m: ["a" => 1]})); t.m.get("a"); });
		run("anon Map<String,Class> unserialized", () -> { var t:TO = haxe.Unserializer.run(haxe.Serializer.run({m: ["a" => new FP(1)]})); t.m.get("a").get(); });
	}
}

# Casts notes §6.5 minus `return` and `closure call` (cast-contexts-working); `Math.random() < 2` became a
# static flag.
--- cast-contexts @gencs
// Where gencs inserts __hx_cast for Dynamic -> Array<Int> (lossy data, so hxc's lossless rule also copies):
// var, argument, static, class field (direct, Reflect.setField, through Dynamic), anonymous field and
// literal, array element, ternary, explicit cast, generic function. Not on `return d` (a plain C# cast:
// InvalidCastException) or a closure call (reflection: ArgumentException). @gencs.
// Those two throwing shapes are in cast-contexts-working: hxc converts there too (a recorded divergence).
typedef TI = {val:Array<Int>};

class C {
	public var ai:Array<Int>;

	public function new() {}
}

class P {
	static var sInt:Array<Int>;
	static var yes = true;

	static function takeInt(a:Array<Int>)
		return Std.string(a);

	static function retInt(d:Dynamic):Array<Int>
		return d;

	static function retIntCast(d:Dynamic):Array<Int>
		return cast d;

	static function gen<T>(a:Array<T>):Array<T>
		return a;

	static function src():Dynamic
		return haxe.Json.parse("[1.5,2]");

	static function run(name:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try {
			Sys.println(name + ": " + Std.string(f()));
		} catch (e:Dynamic) {
			var s = Std.string(e);
			if (s.length > 100) s = s.substr(0, 100);
			Sys.println(name + ": EXC " + s.split("\n")[0].split("\r")[0]);
		}
	}

	static function main() {

		run("ternary", () -> { var r:Array<Int> = yes ? src() : null; Std.string(r); });

# Recorded divergence split from cast-contexts (decision: where gencs throws on a path that should work,

--- cast-contexts-working
// Split from cast-contexts. gencs inserts no __hx_cast on `return d` (a plain C# cast: InvalidCastException)
// or on a closure call (reflection invoke: ArgumentException). hxc converts on both paths, as gencs does for
// `return cast d`, so both print the converted copy [2,2] (lossy data, so a copy). Recorded divergence.
class P {
	static function takeInt(a:Array<Int>)
		return Std.string(a);

	static function retInt(d:Dynamic):Array<Int>
		return d;

	static function src():Dynamic
		return haxe.Json.parse("[1.5,2]");

	static function run(name:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try {
			Sys.println(name + ": " + Std.string(f()));

		}
	}

	static function main() {
		run("return", () -> Std.string(retInt(src())));
		run("closure call", () -> { var f:Array<Int>->String = takeInt; f(src()); });
	}

--- generic-cast-matrix @gencs
// Casts between instantiations for the std-adjacent shapes (std notes §2, §5): G<String> -> G<Int>,
// Dynamic -> Box<Int>, Array<Int> <-> Array<Dynamic>/<Float>/<Null<Int>>, class -> IGet<String>.
// The lossless Array<Dynamic> -> Array<Int> cast followed by a push is in generic-cast-matrix-8314.
class G<T> {
	public var f:T;

}
class Box<T> {
	public var v:T;
	public function new(v:T) this.v = v;
}
interface IGet<T> { function get():T; }
class Cell<T> implements IGet<T> {
	public var v:T;
	public function new(v:T) this.v = v;
	public function get():T return v;
}
class P {
	static function t(n:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {

	static function unwrap<T>(t:T):Box<Int> return cast t;

		t("G<String>->G<Int>", () -> { var g:G<Int> = cast new G<String>("s"); return Std.string(Type.getClass(g)) + " " + g.f; });

		t("G<Float> from G<Int>", () -> { var a = new G<Int>(5); var g:G<Float> = cast a; return Std.string(Type.getClass(g)) + (g == cast a); });
		t("dyn->Box<Int>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new Box(1); var b:Box<Int> = d; return b.v + 1; });
		t("dyn->Box<Int> from Box<String>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new Box("s"); var b:Box<Int> = d; return b.v; });
		t("dyn->Box<Int> from Box<Dyn>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new Box<Dynamic>(4); var b:Box<Int> = d; return Std.string(Type.getClass(b)) + b.v; });
		t("dyn->Box<Dyn> from Box<Int>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new Box<Int>(4); var b:Box<Dynamic> = d; return Std.string(Type.getClass(b)) + b.v + (b == d); });
		t("dyn->Box<String> from Int", () -> { var d:Dynamic = 5; var b:Box<String> = d; return b; });
		t("unwrap(1)", () -> unwrap(1).v);
		t("unwrap(Box<Int>)", () -> { var b = new Box<Int>(2); return unwrap(b).v; });
		t("Array<Int>->Array<Dyn> cast", () -> { var arr = [1]; var dyn:Array<Dynamic> = cast arr; dyn.push(2); return arr.length + "/" + dyn.length + " " + Std.string(Type.getClass(dyn)); });
		t("Array<Int>->Array<Dyn> assign", () -> { var b:Array<Int> = [1]; var c:Array<Dynamic> = b; c.push("x"); return b.length + "/" + c.length; });
		t("Array<Dyn>->Array<Int> bad", () -> { var a:Array<Dynamic> = ["x", 2]; var b:Array<Int> = cast a; return b[0]; });
		t("Array<Dyn>->Array<Int> float", () -> { var a:Array<Dynamic> = [1.5, 2]; var b:Array<Int> = cast a; return b; });
		t("Array<Dyn>->Array<String> int", () -> { var a:Array<Dynamic> = [1, 2]; var b:Array<String> = cast a; return b; });
		t("Array<Int>->Array<Float>", () -> { var a = [1, 2]; var b:Array<Float> = cast a; b.push(0.5); return a.length + "/" + b + Std.string(Type.getClass(b)); });
		t("class->IGet<String>", () -> { var h:IGet<String> = cast new Cell(2); return h.get(); });
		t("class->IGet<Dyn>", () -> { var g:IGet<Dynamic> = new Cell(1); return g.get(); });
		t("Array<Int> -> Array<Null<Int>>", () -> { var a = [1, 2]; var b:Array<Null<Int>> = cast a; b.push(null); return a.length + "/" + b.length; });
		t("Array<Null<Int>> -> Array<Int>", () -> { var a:Array<Null<Int>> = [1, null]; var b:Array<Int> = cast a; return b; });
	}

# Std notes A13: Map-typed instance fields (the server app bulk). cast-map-member covers statics, locals and

--- map-fields-in-classes @gencs
class H {
	var m:Map<String, Int>;
	var im:Map<Int, String>;
	var om:Map<H, Int>;

# Recorded divergence (decision: hxc fixes gencs's parent-cast bug for every parent cast). Types notes
# §8.14 (probe thenable), the three FP -> Th casts of casts' cast-interface, and the Perm, Partial, Both and Fixed
# shapes of types §4's table. Expected [run]: gencs's C# for this program patched with the §4 rule (every
# parent-cast body `return this.X_cast<b1..bn>()`, bk = Pj_c for the first j with aj == Tk), built and run as
# run.sh does (the patcher is fixcasts.py, see verification.md); it rewrote FP.Th_cast, Perm.I2_cast,
# Partial.I2_cast, Both.I1_cast, Both.I2_cast and the std's StringMap.haxe_IMap_cast. Unpatched
# gencs throws InvalidCastException on every line but `same inst` and `Fixed -> I1<Int>`.
--- interface-cast-fixed
// Casts into another instantiation of a generic interface the class implements. gencs's parent cast
// Th_cast<T_c>() calls FP_cast<T>() with the class's own T, so it returns `this` and the castclass after it
// throws InvalidCastException (types notes §4). hxc emits the correct body: FP_cast<T_c>(), Perm_cast<B_c, A_c>(),
// Partial_cast<B_c>(), Both_cast<A_c>(), and in the std StringMap<T> implements IMap<String,T>
// haxe_ds_StringMap_cast<V_c>(); Fixed<T> implements I1<Int> keeps Fixed_cast<T>() as gencs does.
interface Th<T> {
	function then<R>(f:T->R):Th<R>;
	function value():T;
}
class FP<T> implements Th<T> {
	var v:Null<T>;
	public function new(v:T) this.v = v;
	public function then<R>(f:T->R):Th<R> {
		// thenshim's shape: an Any-typed promise cast to Th<R>.
		return cast impl(f);
	}
	function impl(f:Dynamic):FP<Any> return new FP<Any>(f(v));
	public function value():T return v;
}
interface I1<T> { function a():T; }
interface I2<A, B> { function b(x:A):B; }
class Perm<X, Y> implements I2<Y, X> {
	public var x:X;
	public var y:Y;
	public function new(x:X, y:Y) { this.x = x; this.y = y; }
	public function b(v:Y):X return x;
}
class Partial<T> implements I2<String, T> {
	public var t:T;
	public function new(t:T) this.t = t;
	public function b(s:String):T return t;
}
class Both<T> implements I1<T> implements I2<T, T> {
	public var t:T;
	public function new(t:T) this.t = t;
	public function a():T return t;
	public function b(x:T):T return x;
}
class Fixed<T> implements I1<Int> {
	public var t:T;
	public function new(t:T) this.t = t;
	public function a():Int return 1;
}
class P {
	static function t(n:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try Sys.println(n + ": " + f()) catch (e:Dynamic) Sys.println(n + " threw: " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e)));
	}
	static function main() {
		var p = new FP<Int>(20);
		t("then<Int>", () -> { var q:Th<Int> = p.then(x -> x + 1); q.value(); });
		t("dyn->Th<Int>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new FP<Dynamic>(5); var x:Th<Int> = d; x.value(); });
		t("dyn->Th<String>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new FP<Dynamic>("s"); var x:Th<String> = d; x.value(); });
		t("same inst", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new FP<Int>(5); var x:Th<Int> = d; x.value(); });
		t("cast FP<Dyn> -> Th<Int>", () -> { var x:Th<Int> = cast new FP<Dynamic>(1); Std.string(Type.getClass(x)) + " " + x.value(); });
		t("Th<Int> -> Th<Float> cast", () -> { var a:Th<Int> = new FP<Int>(1); var x:Th<Float> = cast a; Std.string(Type.getClass(x)) + " " + x.value(); });
		t("Perm -> I2<String,Int>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new Perm<Dynamic, Dynamic>(1, "s"); var i:I2<String, Int> = d; Std.string(Type.getClass(i)) + " " + i.b("q"); });
		t("Partial -> I2<String,Int>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new Partial<Dynamic>(3); var i:I2<String, Int> = d; Std.string(Type.getClass(i)) + " " + i.b("q"); });
		t("Both -> I1<Int>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new Both<Dynamic>(4); var i:I1<Int> = d; Std.string(Type.getClass(i)) + " " + i.a(); });
		t("Both -> I2<Int,Int>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new Both<Dynamic>(4); var i:I2<Int, Int> = d; Std.string(Type.getClass(i)) + " " + i.b(5); });
		t("Both -> I2<Int,String>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new Both<Dynamic>(4); var i:I2<Int, String> = d; Std.string(Type.getClass(i)); });
		t("IMap from Dynamic", () -> { var sm:Dynamic = new haxe.ds.StringMap<Dynamic>(); var im:haxe.Constraints.IMap<String, Int> = sm; im.set("a", 1); Std.string(Type.getClass(im)) + " " + im.get("a"); });
		t("Fixed -> I1<Int>", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new Fixed<Dynamic>(2); var i:I1<Int> = d; Std.string(Type.getClass(i)) + " " + i.a(); });
	}
}

# Recorded divergence (same decision). Types notes §8.15 (probe supercast) plus the Derived2<A,B> extends
# Base<B> shape of types §4's table. Expected [run]: gencs's C# patched with the §4 rule (GSub.G_cast,
# Base.I1_cast, Derived2.I1_cast and Derived2.Base_cast rewritten), built and run as run.sh does. Unpatched gencs
# throws InvalidCastException on dyn->G<Int>, dyn->Base<Int> and dyn->I1<Int>.
--- superclass-cast-fixed
// The same parent-cast bug on a generic superclass: gencs gives GSub<U> extends G<U> the override
// G_cast<T_c>() { return GSub_cast<U>(); }, which returns `this`, so the cast throws InvalidCastException
// (types notes §4). hxc emits GSub_cast<T_c>(), and for Derived2<A,B> extends Base<B> (whose Base<B> implements
// I1<B>) Derived2_cast<A, T_c>() in both Base_cast<T_c> and I1_cast<T_c>.
class G<T> { public var v:T; public function new(v:T) this.v = v; }
class GSub<U> extends G<U> { public var w:U; public function new(v:U) { super(v); w = v; } }
interface I1<T> { function a():T; }
class Base<T> implements I1<T> {
	public var bv:T;
	public function new(v:T) bv = v;
	public function a():T return bv;
}
class Derived2<A, B> extends Base<B> {
	public var av:A;
	public function new(a:A, b:B) { super(b); av = a; }
}
class P {
	static function t(n:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try Sys.println(n + ": " + f()) catch (e:Dynamic) Sys.println(n + " threw " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e)));
	}
	static function main() {
		var d:Dynamic = new GSub<Dynamic>(5);
		t("dyn->G<Int>", () -> { var g:G<Int> = d; Type.getClass(g) + " v=" + g.v; });
		t("dyn->GSub<Int>", () -> { var s:GSub<Int> = d; Type.getClass(s) + " v=" + s.v + " w=" + s.w; });
		var gs = new GSub<Int>(7);
		var dd:Dynamic = gs;
		var g2:G<Int> = dd;
		Sys.println("same inst: " + (g2 == gs));
		var d2:Dynamic = new Derived2<Dynamic, Dynamic>("x", 5);
		t("dyn->Base<Int>", () -> { var b:Base<Int> = d2; Type.getClass(b) + " " + b.a(); });
		t("dyn->I1<Int>", () -> { var i:I1<Int> = d2; Type.getClass(i) + " " + i.a(); });

		t("dyn->Base<String>", () -> { var b:Base<String> = d2; Type.getClass(b) + " " + b.a(); });
	}

# Casts into abstract-typed places (probes t5probe/abs and t5probe/anon, Task 5). gencs's RealTypeParams sees
# through an abstract to its underlying instantiation, except that a Map-typed anonymous field read used by a
# Map member is C#'s plain cast to IMap<K,V>.
--- abstract-target-casts @gencs
// A Dynamic holding another instantiation, cast into a place typed by an abstract over a generic class:
// Map<String,Int> (whose IMap<string,int> slot gets gencs's StringMap<object>.__hx_cast<int>, a copy) and
// ReadOnlyArray<Int>, as a local, an argument, a field, through Reflect.setField and by `cast`. An anonymous
// field typed Map<String,Int> is read with C#'s cast to IMap<string,int> before a Map member (InvalidCastException
// for a StringMap<object>), but goes through __hx_cast when it is stored first (`var m = a.m`).
import haxe.ds.ReadOnlyArray;

typedef A = {m:Map<String, Int>, ro:ReadOnlyArray<Int>, sm:haxe.ds.StringMap<Int>, mo:Map<String, Array<Int>>};

class H {
	public var m:Map<String, Int>;
	public var ro:ReadOnlyArray<Int>;

	public function new() {}
}

class P {
	static function run(name:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try Sys.println(name + ": " + Std.string(f())) catch (e:Dynamic) Sys.println(name + ": EXC " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e)));
	}

	static function takeMap(m:Map<String, Int>) return m.get("a");

	static function main() {
		run("local Map", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new haxe.ds.StringMap<Dynamic>(); var m:Map<String, Int> = d; m.set("a", 1); m.get("a"); });
		run("arg Map", () -> { var sm = new haxe.ds.StringMap<Dynamic>(); sm.set("a", 1); var d:Dynamic = sm; takeMap(d); });
		run("field Map", () -> { var h = new H(); var d:Dynamic = new haxe.ds.StringMap<Dynamic>(); h.m = d; h.m.set("a", 2); h.m.get("a"); });
		run("setField Map", () -> { var h = new H(); Reflect.setField(h, "m", new haxe.ds.StringMap<Dynamic>()); h.m.set("a", 3); h.m.get("a"); });
		run("cast Map", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new haxe.ds.StringMap<Dynamic>(); var m = (cast d : Map<String, Int>); m.set("a", 4); m.get("a"); });
		run("local ROA", () -> { var d:Dynamic = haxe.Json.parse("[1,2]"); var r:ReadOnlyArray<Int> = d; r[0]; });
		run("field ROA", () -> { var h = new H(); var d:Dynamic = haxe.Json.parse("[1,2]"); h.ro = d; h.ro[1]; });
		var sm = new haxe.ds.StringMap<Dynamic>();
		sm.set("a", 1);
		var d:Dynamic = {m: sm, ro: haxe.Json.parse("[3]"), sm: sm, mo: sm};
		var a:A = d;
		run("anon Map", () -> a.m.get("a"));
		run("anon Map for", () -> { var n = 0; for (k => v in a.m) n += v; n; });
		run("anon Map var", () -> { var m = a.m; m.exists("a"); });
		run("anon ROA", () -> a.ro[0]);
		run("anon StringMap", () -> a.sm.get("a"));
		run("anon Map erased", () -> a.mo.exists("a"));
	}
}

# The same with an abstract over a generic interface, a typed IMap, and `return d` (Decision 4). gencs's parent
# cast (FP.Th_cast, StringMap.haxe_IMap_cast) returns `this`, so plain gencs throws InvalidCastException on all 7
# lines; hxc's copies (decision 2 of plan 3c).
# Provenance: plain Haxe 4.3.7 gencs prints `EXC System.InvalidCastException` for each line; the same C# with its
# parent casts rewritten by docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-25-dotnet-generic-instantiations/fixcasts.py prints this
# expectation except `ret Map: EXC System.InvalidCastException` (`return d` stays C#'s plain cast there).
--- abstract-target-casts-fixed
// Casts into places typed by an abstract over a generic interface (Pr<Int> over Th<Int>) and by IMap<String,Int>
// itself, from a Dynamic holding the object instantiation, and `return d` into a Map<String,Int>. gencs throws
// InvalidCastException on each (its parent casts return `this`; `return d` is a plain cast); hxc's __hx_cast
// copies into the instantiation asked for. Recorded divergence.
interface Th<T> {
	function get():T;
}

class FP<T> implements Th<T> {
	var v:T;

	public function new(v:T)
		this.v = v;

	public function get():T
		return v;
}

abstract Pr<T>(Th<T>) from Th<T> to Th<T> {
	public function get():T
		return this.get();
}

typedef A = {p:Pr<Int>, im:haxe.Constraints.IMap<String, Int>, th:Th<Int>};

class H {
	public var p:Pr<Int>;

	public function new() {}
}

class P {
	static function run(name:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try Sys.println(name + ": " + Std.string(f())) catch (e:Dynamic) Sys.println(name + ": EXC " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e)));
	}

	static function retMap(d:Dynamic):Map<String, Int>
		return d;

	static function main() {
		run("local Pr", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new FP<Dynamic>(5); var p:Pr<Int> = d; p.get(); });
		run("field Pr", () -> { var h = new H(); var d:Dynamic = new FP<Dynamic>(6); h.p = d; h.p.get(); });
		run("local IMap", () -> { var d:Dynamic = new haxe.ds.StringMap<Dynamic>(); var m:haxe.Constraints.IMap<String, Int> = d; m.set("a", 7); m.get("a"); });
		run("ret Map", () -> { var sm = new haxe.ds.StringMap<Dynamic>(); sm.set("a", 8); retMap(sm).get("a"); });
		var sm = new haxe.ds.StringMap<Dynamic>();
		sm.set("a", 1);
		var d:Dynamic = {p: new FP<Dynamic>(2), im: sm, th: new FP<Dynamic>(4)};
		var a:A = d;
		run("anon Pr", () -> a.p.get());
		run("anon IMap", () -> a.im.get("a"));
		run("anon Th", () -> a.th.get());
	}
}

# Types notes §8.9 (probe access): G<Dynamic>, Array<Dynamic> and Map<String,Dynamic> members, typed ->

--- companion-access @gencs
// Member access through a companion-interface-typed value (G<Dynamic>, Array<Dynamic>, StringMap<Dynamic>).
class G<T> {

		var f = a.filter(x -> x != null);

# Casts notes §6.2. No line needed splitting: its two throws (a string pushed into an Array<Int> held as
# Array<Dynamic>, an Int pushed into an Array<String> one) come from genericCast on the typed array, which hxc
# reproduces with companion typing; no line is a gencs throw on a path hxc makes work.
--- cast-array-view @gencs
// A typed Array<X> passed as Array<Dynamic>: gencs passes the same object (Array<Dynamic> is the companion
// interface), so writes reach the caller's array and a wrong-typed write throws from genericCast. @gencs.
// An element write `a[i] = v` through the Array<Dynamic> goes through the companion's indexer, whose setter
// casts v to the element type and throws for a wrong-typed one.
class P {
	static var sDyn:Array<Dynamic>;

	static function takeDyn(a:Array<Dynamic>) {
		a.push(99);
		a[0] = 42;
	}

	static function takeDynStr(a:Array<Dynamic>)
		a.push("s");

	static function retDyn(a:Array<Int>):Array<Dynamic>
		return a;

	static function run(name:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try {
			Sys.println(name + ": " + Std.string(f()));
		} catch (e:Dynamic) {
			var s = Std.string(e);
			if (s.length > 100) s = s.substr(0, 100);
			Sys.println(name + ": EXC " + s.split("\n")[0].split("\r")[0]);
		}
	}

	static function main() {
		run("arg", () -> { var ai = [1, 2, 3]; takeDyn(ai); Std.string(ai); });
		run("arg wrong type", () -> { var ai = [1, 2, 3]; takeDynStr(ai); Std.string(ai); });
		run("local", () -> { var ai = [1, 2, 3]; var d:Array<Dynamic> = ai; d.push(4); Std.string(ai) + " " + (d == ai) + " " + Std.string(Type.typeof(d)); });
		run("return", () -> { var ai = [1, 2, 3]; var d = retDyn(ai); d.push(4); Std.string(ai); });
		run("static", () -> { var ai = [1, 2, 3]; sDyn = ai; sDyn.push(4); Std.string(ai); });
		run("closure", () -> { var f:Array<Dynamic>->Void = takeDyn; var ai = [1, 2]; f(ai); Std.string(ai); });
		run("push 1.5 and '7' into int", () -> { var ai = [1]; var d:Array<Dynamic> = ai; d.push(1.5); d.push("7"); Std.string(ai); });
		run("cast Str->Dyn push int", () -> { var ids = ["a", "b"]; var params:Array<Dynamic> = cast ids.copy(); params.push(5); Std.string(params); });
		run("Dynamic write wrong", () -> { var ai = [1, 2]; var d:Dynamic = ai; d[0] = 2.5; d.push("7"); Std.string(ai); });
		run("Box<Int> as Box<Dynamic>", () -> { var b = new Box<Int>(1); var t:Box<Dynamic> = b; t.v = 2.5; b.v; });
		run("index write float into int", () -> { var ai = [1, 2]; var a:Array<Dynamic> = ai; a[1] = 3.7; Std.string(ai); });
		run("index write string into int", () -> { var ai = [1, 2]; var a:Array<Dynamic> = ai; a[1] = "q"; Std.string(ai); });
	}
}

class Box<T> {
	public var v:T;

	public function new(v:T)
		this.v = v;
}

# Types notes §8.6 (probe companion).
--- generic-reflection @gencs
// Companion interfaces: reflection over them, generic subclassing, generic interfaces.
class G<T> {
	public var v:T;
	public var n:Int = 7;
	public function new(v:T) this.v = v;
	public function get():T return v;
	public function plain():Int return n;
	public function str():String return "G.str";
}
class Sub extends G<Int> {
	public var w:String = "w";
	public function new() super(5);
	public function own():String return w;
}
class GSub<U> extends G<U> {
	public var u:U;
	public function new(x:U) { super(x); u = x; }
	public function getU():U return u;
}
interface IG<T> {
	function ig():T;
	function igPlain():Int;
}
class GI<T> implements IG<T> {
	public var x:T;
	public function new(x:T) this.x = x;
	public function ig():T return x;
	public function igPlain():Int return 3;
}
class NI implements IG<String> {
	public function new() {}
	public function ig():String return "ni";
	public function igPlain():Int return 4;
}
class P {
	static function main() {
		var keep = new haxe.ds.StringMap<Int>(); keep.set("a", 1);
		Sys.println("resolve G: " + Type.resolveClass("G"));
		Sys.println("resolve name: " + Type.getClassName(Type.resolveClass("G")));
		Sys.println("resolve Array: " + Type.resolveClass("Array") + " / " + Type.getClassName(Type.resolveClass("Array")));
		Sys.println("resolve StringMap: " + Type.resolveClass("haxe.ds.StringMap") + " / " + Type.getClassName(Type.resolveClass("haxe.ds.StringMap")));
		Sys.println("resolve Sub: " + Type.resolveClass("Sub"));
		Sys.println("resolve GSub: " + Type.resolveClass("GSub"));
		Sys.println("resolve IG: " + Type.resolveClass("IG"));
		Sys.println("fields G: " + Type.getInstanceFields(G));
		Sys.println("fields Sub: " + Type.getInstanceFields(Sub));
		Sys.println("fields GSub: " + Type.getInstanceFields(GSub));
		Sys.println("fields GI: " + Type.getInstanceFields(GI));
		Sys.println("fields NI: " + Type.getInstanceFields(NI));
		Sys.println("fields Array: " + Type.getInstanceFields(Array));
		Sys.println("fields resolved G: " + Type.getInstanceFields(Type.resolveClass("G")));
		Sys.println("fields resolved Array: " + Type.getInstanceFields(Type.resolveClass("Array")));
		Sys.println("class fields G: " + Type.getClassFields(G));

--- list-lambda-generics @gencs

# Std notes §3.1: Std.downcast, Std.instance and cs.Lib.as of a generic class are `as` its companion, and an

# (probe t7probe/mono: `global::Box r = bx as global::Box`, `global::Array a = new Array<object>(…)`).
--- downcast-generic-class @gencs
class Box<T> {
	public var v:T;
	public function new(v:T) this.v = v;

	public function new() {}
}

	static function main() {
		var bx:Dynamic = new Box<Int>(1);
		var pt:Dynamic = new Pt();
		var a = [];
		Sys.println(a);

		Sys.println(r != null);
		Sys.println(Std.downcast(pt, Box) != null);

# Std notes L7, B7. The method list is sorted with a comparator that returns 0 for equal strings; the
# researcher's `a < b ? -1 : 1` made hxcs's quicksort leave the list in an order that depends on its input
# (GetMethods order), so its QDyn list was unsorted.
--- explicit-impl-erased-generic-interface @gencs
class Pt { public var x:Int = 0; public function new() {} public function toString() return "Pt"; }
interface IQ<T> { function get(i:Int):T; function put(v:T):Void; var last(default, null):T; }
class QPt implements IQ<Pt> {
	public var last(default, null):Pt;
	public function new() {}
	public function get(i:Int):Pt return last;
	public function put(v:Pt):Void last = v;
}
class QInt implements IQ<Int> {
	public var last(default, null):Int = 0;
	public function new() {}
	public function get(i:Int):Int return last + i;
	public function put(v:Int):Void last = v;
}
class QArr implements IQ<Array<Int>> {
	public var last(default, null):Array<Int>;
	public function new() {}
	public function get(i:Int):Array<Int> return last;
	public function put(v:Array<Int>):Void last = v;
}
class QDyn implements IQ<Dynamic> {
	public var last(default, null):Dynamic;
	public function new() {}
	public function get(i:Int):Dynamic return last;
	public function put(v:Dynamic):Void last = v;
}
class P {
	static function t(n:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try Sys.println(n + " " + f()) catch (e:Dynamic) Sys.println(n + " EXC " + (Std.isOfType(e, String) ? "String " + e : Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e))));
	}
	static function main() {
		var q:IQ<Pt> = new QPt();
		q.put(new Pt());
		t("QPt get", () -> q.get(0));
		var qi:IQ<Int> = new QInt();
		qi.put(4);
		t("QInt get", () -> qi.get(2));
		var qa:IQ<Array<Int>> = new QArr();
		qa.put([1]);
		t("QArr get", () -> qa.get(0));
		var qd:IQ<Dynamic> = new QDyn();
		qd.put("d");
		t("QDyn get", () -> qd.get(0));
		for (c in ([QPt, QInt, QArr, QDyn] : Array<Class<Dynamic>>)) {
			var cls:Class<Dynamic> = c;
			t("fields " + Type.getClassName(cls), () -> {
				var fl:cs.Flags<cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags> = new cs.Flags(cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Instance) | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Public | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly;
				var ms = [for (m in cs.Lib.toNativeType(cls).GetMethods(fl)) Std.string(m) + (m.IsPublic ? " public" : " nonpublic") ];
				ms.sort((a, b) -> a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0);
				return "\n  " + ms.join("\n  ");
			});
		}
		t("dyn call", () -> Reflect.callMethod(q, Reflect.field(q, "get"), [0]));
		t("dyn field", () -> Reflect.field(q, "last"));
	}
}

--- erased-interface-overload-shapes @gencs
// gencs's overloads for erased generic interfaces (types notes §3): an overload of a method the class
// declares comes in front of it, one of an inherited method or an explicit implementation in front of
// the class's fields, after the static __hx_cast, the last made first; a final class's overload is
// final; a class whose superclass already has the overload gets none, and an interface's own
// interfaces get them too. A class listing an interface its superclass implements has a cast of its own
// (S, and NI2 with an interface erasure does not change).
class C { public function new() {} public function toString() return "C"; }
interface IQ<T> { function f(x:T):T; function h(x:T, n:Int):Void; function get():T; }
interface IQ2<T> extends IQ<T> { function k(x:T):Void; }
interface IR<T> { function f(x:T):T; }
class B {
	public function new() {}
	public function f(x:C):C return x;
	public function h(x:C, n:Int):Void Sys.println("B.h " + n);
	public function get():C return new C();
}
class Q2 extends B implements IQ<C> {
	public function new() super();
	public function own():Int return 1;
}
class GX<T> extends B implements IQ<C> {
	public var t:T;
	public function new() super();
}
class Q implements IQ<C> implements IR<C> {
	public function new() {}
	public function f(x:C):C { Sys.println("Q.f"); return x; }
	public function h(x:C, n:Int):Void Sys.println("Q.h " + n);
	public function get():C return new C();
}
class S extends Q implements IQ<C> {
	public function new() super();
	override public function f(x:C):C { Sys.println("S.f"); return x; }
}
final class F implements IQ<C> {
	public function new() {}
	public function f(x:C):C return x;
	public function h(x:C, n:Int):Void Sys.println("F.h " + n);
	public function get():C return new C();
}
class X<T> implements IQ2<C> {
	public var t:T;
	public function new() {}
	public function f(x:C):C return x;
	public function h(x:C, n:Int):Void Sys.println("X.h " + n);
	public function get():C return new C();
	public function k(x:C):Void Sys.println("X.k");
}
interface IG<T> { function a():T; }
class NI implements IG<String> { public function new() {} public function a():String return "a"; }
class NI2 extends NI implements IG<String> { public function new() super(); }
class P {
	static function methods(c:Class<Dynamic>):String {
		var fl:cs.Flags<cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags> = new cs.Flags(cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Instance) | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Public | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly;
		var ms = [
			for (m in cs.Lib.toNativeType(c).GetMethods(fl))
				if (!StringTools.startsWith(m.Name, "__hx_") && !StringTools.endsWith(m.Name, "_cast"))
					Std.string(m) + (m.IsPublic ? " public" : " nonpublic") + (m.IsVirtual ? " virtual" : "") + (m.IsFinal ? " final" : "")
		];
		ms.sort((a, b) -> a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0);
		return "\n  " + ms.join("\n  ");
	}
	static function main() {
		var qs:Array<IQ<C>> = [new Q(), new S(), new F(), new X<Int>()];
		for (q in qs) {
			Sys.println(q.f(new C()));
			q.h(new C(), 2);
			Sys.println(q.get());
		}
		var x:IQ2<C> = new X<String>();
		x.k(new C());
		var r:IR<C> = new S();
		Sys.println(r.f(new C()));
		for (c in ([Q2, GX, Q, F, X] : Array<Class<Dynamic>>))
			Sys.println(Type.getClassName(c) + " " + Type.getInstanceFields(c) + methods(c));
		Sys.println("S " + Type.getInstanceFields(S) + methods(S));
		Sys.println("NI2 " + Type.getInstanceFields(NI2));
		var ig:IG<String> = new NI2();
		Sys.println(ig.a());
	}
}

# gencs's C# for this overflows the stack (types notes §3: its overload calls itself), so its [run] is

--- erased-interface-inherited-implementation
// An erased interface's method implemented by an inherited method: gencs's overload `object f(object x)
// { return this.f((C) x); }` calls itself, C# picking the overload of the most derived class, until the
// stack overflows. hxc's calls the inherited method.
class C { public function new() {} public function toString() return "C"; }
interface IQ<T> { function f(x:T):T; function h(x:T, n:Int):Void; }
class B {
	public function new() {}
	public function f(x:C):C return x;
	public function h(x:C, n:Int):Void Sys.println("B.h " + n);
}
class Q2 extends B implements IQ<C> {
	public function new() super();
}
class GX<T> extends B implements IQ<C> {
	public function new() super();
}
class O extends Q2 {
	public function new() super();
	override public function f(x:C):C { Sys.println("O.f"); return x; }
}
class P {
	static function main() {
		var qs:Array<IQ<C>> = [new Q2(), new GX<Int>(), new O()];
		for (q in qs) {
			Sys.println(q.f(new C()));
			q.h(new C(), 1);
		}
	}
}

--- overloaded-override-erased-signature @gencs
// An @:overload'ed method of a generic superclass overridden through an erased type argument (S extends
// G<C> overriding f(x:C), whose slot is G`1<object>'s f(object)): as gencs's FixOverrides writes it, an
// override with the slot's signature calls the method, which becomes a new virtual overload. gencs does
// the same for a further @:overload override (T's) and calls each through the overload's slot, so a T
// held as an S runs T's method. Each overriding class has its own __hx_invokeField case, which calls the
// overload's slot with the arguments as they come.
class C { public function new() {} public function toString() return "C"; }
class G<T> {
	public function new() {}
	@:overload public function f(x:T):String return "G.f(T)";
	@:overload public function f(x:Int, y:Int):String return "G.f(Int,Int)";
}
class S extends G<C> {
	public function new() super();
	@:overload override public function f(x:C):String return "S.f(C) " + x;
}
class T extends S {
	public function new() super();
	@:overload override public function f(x:C):String return "T.f(C) " + x;
	public function more():String return "more";
}
class P {
	static function tr(n:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try Sys.println(n + " " + f()) catch (e:Dynamic) Sys.println(n + " EXC " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e)));
	}
	static function main() {
		var s = new S();
		Sys.println(s.f(new C()));
		Sys.println(s.f(1, 2));
		var g:G<C> = s;
		Sys.println(g.f(new C()));
		var t:G<C> = new T();
		Sys.println(t.f(new C()));
		var st:S = new T();
		Sys.println(st.f(new C()));
		var d:Dynamic = s;
		Sys.println(d.f(new C()));
		tr("s dyn2", () -> d.f(1, 2));
		tr("t refl1", () -> Reflect.callMethod(st, Reflect.field(st, "f"), [new C()]));
		tr("t refl2", () -> Reflect.callMethod(st, Reflect.field(st, "f"), [1, 2]));
		var dt:Dynamic = st;
		tr("t dyn2", () -> dt.f(1, 2));
		Sys.println(Type.getInstanceFields(S));
		Sys.println(Type.getInstanceFields(T));
		var fl:cs.Flags<cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags> = new cs.Flags(cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Instance) | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Public | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly;
		for (c in ([S, T] : Array<Class<Dynamic>>)) {
			var ms = [
				for (m in cs.Lib.toNativeType(c).GetMethods(fl))
					Std.string(m) + (m.IsPublic ? " public" : " nonpublic") + (m.IsVirtual ? " virtual" : "")
						+ (Std.string(m.Attributes).indexOf("VtableLayoutMask") >= 0 ? " newslot" : "")
			];
			ms.sort((a, b) -> a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0);
			Sys.println(Type.getClassName(c) + "\n  " + ms.join("\n  "));
		}
	}
}

# Q.get's Haxe signature is Array's companion, I`1<object>.get's is Array`1<object>, so Q gets an explicit
# implementation that casts it, which the CLR needs to load Q; `i.get()` through I<Dynamic> goes through
# __hx_invokeField, not through it. gencs's C# for it fails with CS0738, so the case is not @gencs and its
# [run] is hand-written.
--- erased-interface-dynamic-argument
interface I<T> {
	function get():Array<T>;
	function one():T;
}
class Q implements I<Dynamic> {
	public function new() {}
	public function get():Array<Dynamic> return [1, "a"];
	public function one():Dynamic return 5;
}
class P {
	static function main() {
		var q = new Q();
		var i:I<Dynamic> = q;
		Sys.println(i.get());
		Sys.println(i.one());
		Sys.println(q.get());
	}
}

--- relisted-interface-casts @gencs
// A class that lists a generic interface has a cast of its own for it (a new slot returning this), even
// when its superclass has one: deep (NI3's IG through IG2), in the order it lists them (NI4), and not when
// it lists nothing (NI5). A generic class overrides the inherited cast instead (GS).
interface IG<T> { function a():T; }
interface IG2<T> extends IG<T> { function b():T; }
interface IH<T> { function h():T; }
class NI implements IG<String> { public function new() {} public function a():String return "a"; }
class NI2 extends NI implements IG<String> { public function new() super(); }
class NI3 extends NI implements IG2<String> { public function new() super(); public function b():String return "b"; }
class NI4 extends NI implements IH<Int> implements IG<String> { public function new() super(); public function h():Int return 1; }
class NI5 extends NI2 { public function new() super(); }
class NI6 extends NI2 implements IG<String> { public function new() super(); }
class GB<T> implements IG<T> { public function new() {} public function a():T return null; }

--- cast-array-convert @gencs
// Array<Dynamic> -> Array<X> where an element does not convert losslessly: a copy through genericCast in
// gencs and (by the lossless fallback) in hxc. Prints only the converted values. @gencs.
class P {
	static function toInts(a:Array<Dynamic>):Array<Int> {
		var r:Array<Int> = cast a;
		return r;
	}

	static function toFloats(a:Array<Dynamic>):Array<Float> {
		var r:Array<Float> = cast a;
		return r;
	}

	static function toBools(a:Array<Dynamic>):Array<Bool> {
		var r:Array<Bool> = cast a;
		return r;
	}

	static function toStrs(a:Array<Dynamic>):Array<String> {
		var r:Array<String> = cast a;
		return r;
	}

	static function run(name:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try {
			Sys.println(name + ": " + Std.string(f()));
		} catch (e:Dynamic) {
			var s = Std.string(e);
			if (s.length > 100) s = s.substr(0, 100);
			Sys.println(name + ": EXC " + s.split("\n")[0].split("\r")[0]);
		}
	}

	static function main() {
		run("int<-halves", () -> toInts([0.5, 1.5, 2.5, -0.5, -1.5, 1.4, 1.6]));
		run("int<-null", () -> toInts([null, 1]));
		run("int<-big", () -> toInts([1e10]));
		run("int<-nan", () -> toInts([Math.NaN]));
		run("int<-Int64", () -> toInts([haxe.Int64.make(0, 5)]));
		run("int<-bool", () -> toInts([true, false]));
		run("int<-str", () -> toInts(["7", " 8 "]));
		run("int<-badstr", () -> toInts(["1.5"]));
		run("int<-obj", () -> toInts([{}]));
		run("int<-date", () -> toInts([Date.fromTime(0)]));
		run("float<-null", () -> toFloats([null, 1]));
		run("float<-str", () -> toFloats(["1.5"]));
		run("float<-bool", () -> toFloats([true]));
		run("bool<-int", () -> toBools([1]));
		run("bool<-null", () -> toBools([null, true]));
		run("str<-int", () -> toStrs([1]));
		run("str<-obj", () -> toStrs([{}]));
		run("single", () -> { var r:Array<Single> = haxe.Json.parse("[1.1, null]"); Std.string(r); });
		run("int64", () -> { var r:Array<haxe.Int64> = haxe.Json.parse("[1.6]"); Std.string(r); });
	}
}

			Sys.println(name + ": " + Std.string(f()));

--- cast-array-forward-eq
// Equality across an Array and its forward besides #4872's Array<Dynamic>. A typed Array`1<object> (an
// Array<Null<Int>>, an Array<Any>) against an Array of a basic element compares through Runtime.eq, as an
// Array<Dynamic> does; two unrelated arrays and two of one CLR type stay a comparison of references. `cast ni`
// back to Array<Null<Int>> copies, in gencs too, so that comparison is false. A closure compares its object
// with refEq and an enum argument with Equals, so Reflect.compareMethods and Type.enumEq see one array, and so
// does haxe.lang.Closure's Equals override, which compares the objects through Runtime.eq.

	W(a:Dynamic);

		var p:Array<Null<Int>> = [1], q:Array<Int> = [1];

# Review Focus 3 of plan 3c: Array's surface to C# and to reflection, get_Item and set_Item of gencs's Array
# indexer (its __get/__set rule) included.
--- array-clr-surface @gencs
// Array`1 keeps its namespace, name and arity, and `length` stays a public Int32 field (the server app's C# builds
// `new Array<string>()` and reads `.length`). The #8314 forward's members (__hx_fwd, __hx_from) never show
// in Reflect.fields, Type.getInstanceFields or haxe.Serializer output, for a plain unserialized array, one a
// typed cast has reinterpreted, or the typed array itself. The Array companion interface declares gencs's
// methods, in order, and nothing of the forward's. @gencs.
class P {
	static function main() {
		var t = cs.Lib.toNativeType(Array);
		Sys.println(t.Namespace + " " + t.Name + " " + t.GetGenericArguments().Length);
		var f = t.GetField("length");
		Sys.println(f.Name + " " + f.IsPublic + " " + f.FieldType.Name);
		var plain:Array<Dynamic> = haxe.Unserializer.run("ai1i2i3h");
		var a:Array<Dynamic> = haxe.Unserializer.run("ai1i2i3h");
		var b:Array<Int> = cast a;
		Sys.println(Reflect.fields(plain) + " " + Reflect.fields(a) + " " + Reflect.fields(b));
		Sys.println(Type.getInstanceFields(Array));
		Sys.println(haxe.Serializer.run(a) + " " + haxe.Serializer.run(b) + " " + haxe.Serializer.run({a: a, b: b}));
		var companion = cs.system.Type._GetType("Array");
		var ms = companion.GetMethods(new cs.Flags(cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Public) | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Instance
			| cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly);
		Sys.println(companion.IsInterface + " " + [for (i in 0...ms.Length) ms[i].Name]);
	}
}

# Review Focus 1 of plan 3c: the first cast of one unserialized array from many threads at once. Haxe code
# can't start a thread until milestone 4 (cast-array-threads, m4.cases.txt), so HxcCheck's stress-arrayforward
# drives P.make and P.toInts from C#: 200 rounds of 8 threads behind a barrier, each casting one fresh array
# and pushing onto what it got. Every thread must get the same Array`1<int>, with 3 + 8 elements, and the
# original's length must follow it. Two more shapes run 1000 rounds of 3 pushes a thread: makeFull's array
# fills its capacity, and makeStrings's (cast with toStrings) holds a null, which converts losslessly into
# String; in both an install racing the scan would read past the original's storage. makeMixed's [1.5,2]
# runs 5000 rounds of two target types racing: four threads cast it with toFloats, which reinterprets it, and
# push, while four cast it with toInts, which copies it (1.5 is lossy); a copy that took the original's length
# after those pushes but its stale storage would read past that storage.
--- array-forward-race @stress-arrayforward
class P {
	public static function make():Array<Dynamic> {
		return haxe.Unserializer.run("ai1i2i3h");
	}

	public static function makeFull():Array<Dynamic> {
		return haxe.Unserializer.run("ai1i2i3i4h");
	}

	public static function makeStrings():Array<Dynamic> {
		return haxe.Unserializer.run("ay1:any1:bh");
	}

	public static function makeMixed():Array<Dynamic> {
		return haxe.Unserializer.run("ad1.5i2h");
	}

	public static function toInts(a:Dynamic):Array<Int> {
		return a;
	}

	public static function toStrings(a:Dynamic):Array<String> {
		return a;
	}

	public static function toFloats(a:Dynamic):Array<Float> {
		return a;
	}

	static function main() {
		Sys.println("ok");
	}
}

# Std notes A3. The timer and the event run in the exit loop, so the sleep only makes the timer due.
--- timer-and-main-thread @gencs
import sys.thread.Thread;

class P {
	static function main() {
		var cur = Thread.current();
		Sys.println(cur != null);
		Sys.println(Thread.current() == cur);
		var t0 = haxe.Timer.stamp();

		Sys.println(haxe.Timer.stamp() >= t0);

# Std notes A8. toString and both Printer lines use a one-attribute document: attribute order follows
# String.GetHashCode, which .NET randomizes per process (the researcher's `<a c="2" b="1">` was one ordering).
# The attribute names are sorted with a comparator that returns 0 for equal strings (see http-response-reading).
--- xml-attributes @gencs
// Xml's attributeMap is a Map<String,String> field, so every attribute access is the Map abstract's identity
// downcast (std notes §1.A8). Attribute order in toString/Printer follows String.GetHashCode, which .NET
// randomizes per process, so those lines print a one-attribute document.
class P {
	static function t(n:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try Sys.println(n + " " + f()) catch (e:Dynamic) Sys.println(n + " EXC " + (Std.isOfType(e, String) ? "String " + e : Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e))));
	}
	static function main() {
		var x = Xml.parse("<a b='1' c='2'><d e='x'/>text</a>");
		var a = x.firstElement();
		var y = Xml.parse("<r k='v'><d e='x'/>text</r>");
		t("nodeName", () -> a.nodeName);
		t("get b", () -> a.get("b"));
		t("get z", () -> a.get("z"));
		t("exists c", () -> a.exists("c"));
		t("exists z", () -> a.exists("z"));
		t("attributes", () -> { var l = []; for (k in a.attributes()) l.push(k); l.sort((p, q) -> p < q ? -1 : p > q ? 1 : 0); l.join(","); });
		t("set", () -> { a.set("z", "9"); a.get("z"); });
		t("remove", () -> { a.remove("z"); a.exists("z"); });
		t("toString", () -> y.toString());
		t("elements", () -> [for (e in a.elements()) e.nodeName].join(","));
		t("access", () -> { var ac = new haxe.xml.Access(a); ac.att.b + ac.node.d.att.e; });
		t("printer", () -> haxe.xml.Printer.print(y));
		t("printer pretty", () -> haxe.xml.Printer.print(y, true));
	}
}

# Std notes A6 (a fake socket, no network), without customRequest: its URL parsing calls EReg.matched, a
# .NET indexer (milestone 4), so http-response-parsing waits in m4.cases.txt. This calls readHttpResponse,
# customRequest's own step once the request is written, with its error handling. getResponseHeaderValues
# throws NullReferenceException in gencs when no header repeated (responseHeadersSameKey is null), a gencs
# bug the spec reproduces (Decision 5); the eof run pins it. The header names are sorted with a comparator
# that returns 0 for equal strings: with `a < b ? -1 : 1`, hxcs's quicksort gave an order that followed the
# StringMap's per-process key order.
--- http-response-reading @gencs
import haxe.io.Bytes;
import haxe.io.BytesInput;
import haxe.io.BytesOutput;

class Fake extends sys.net.Socket {
	public function new(response:String) {
		super();
		@:privateAccess this.input = new BytesInput(Bytes.ofString(response));
		@:privateAccess this.output = new BytesOutput();
	}
	override public function setTimeout(t:Float):Void {}
	override public function shutdown(r:Bool, w:Bool):Void {}
	override public function close():Void {}
}

class P {
	static function run(name:String, response:String) {
		var h = new sys.Http("http://127.0.0.1:8080/path?x=1");
		var out = new BytesOutput();
		var status = -1;
		h.onStatus = s -> status = s;
		h.onError = e -> Sys.println(name + " error: " + e);
		h.onData = d -> Sys.println(name + " data: " + d);
		// customRequest's own steps after the request is written: its URL parsing calls EReg.matched.
		try @:privateAccess h.readHttpResponse(out, new Fake(response)) catch (e:Dynamic) h.onError(Std.string(e));
		Sys.println(name + " status " + status);
		if (h.responseHeaders == null) { Sys.println(name + " no headers"); return; }
		var keys = [for (k in h.responseHeaders.keys()) k];
		keys.sort((a, b) -> a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0);
		Sys.println(name + " headers " + keys.map(k -> k + "=" + h.responseHeaders.get(k)).join(";"));
		if (name == "len") Sys.println(name + " multi " + h.getResponseHeaderValues("Set-Cookie") + " " + h.getResponseHeaderValues("X-B") + " " + h.getResponseHeaderValues("none"));
		if (name == "eof") Sys.println(name + " none " + (try Std.string(h.getResponseHeaderValues("none")) catch (e:Dynamic) "EXC " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e))));
		Sys.println(name + " body " + out.getBytes().toString());
	}
	static function main() {
		run("len", "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\nX-B: b\r\nSet-Cookie: a=1\r\nSet-Cookie: b=2\r\n\r\nhello");
		run("eof", "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nX-C: c\r\n\r\nuntil end");
		run("404", "HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\nContent-Length: 2\r\n\r\nno");
		run("bad", "garbage\r\n\r\n");
	}
}
===

# Std notes §4. The Unserializer's ArgumentException on E.A/E.B/E.D constructor arguments is a gencs bug the
# spec reproduces.
--- serialize-generic-values @gencs
class Box<T> {
	public var v:T;
	public function new(v:T) this.v = v;
	public function get():T return v;
}
class Sub extends Box<Int> {
	public var z:Int = 3;
	public function new() super(1);
}
class Pt {
	public var x:Int = 0;
	public function new() {}
}
class Pair<A, B> {
	public var a:A; public var b:B;
	public function new(a:A, b:B) { this.a = a; this.b = b; }
}
enum E { A(a:Array<Int>); B(m:Map<String, Int>); C(o:haxe.ds.Option<Int>); D(b:Box<Int>); N; }
class Holder {
	public var ai:Array<Int> = [1, 2];
	public var af:Array<Float> = [1.5];
	public var an:Array<Null<Int>> = [1, null];
	public var sm:Map<String, Int> = ["k" => 4];
	public var im:Map<Int, String> = [7 => "seven"];
	public var li:List<String> = new List();
	public var bx:Box<Int> = new Box(9);
	public var bn:Box<Null<Int>> = new Box(null);
	public var sa:Map<String, Array<Int>> = ["z" => [1]];
	public var om:haxe.ds.ObjectMap<Pt, Int> = new haxe.ds.ObjectMap();
	public function new() { li.add("x"); }
}
class P {
	static function t(n:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try Sys.println(n + " " + f()) catch (e:Dynamic) Sys.println(n + " EXC " + (Std.isOfType(e, String) ? "String " + e : Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e))));
	}
	static function rt(n:String, v:Dynamic) {
		var s:String = null;
		t("ser " + n, () -> s = haxe.Serializer.run(v));
		if (s == null) return;
		t("unser " + n, () -> { var u:Dynamic = haxe.Unserializer.run(s); return Std.string(Type.getClass(u)) + " " + Std.string(u); });
		t("reser " + n, () -> haxe.Serializer.run(haxe.Unserializer.run(s)));
	}
	static function main() {
		rt("Box<Int>", new Box<Int>(1));
		rt("Box<String>", new Box<String>("s"));
		rt("Box<Null<Int>> null", new Box<Null<Int>>(null));
		rt("Box<Null<Int>> 5", new Box<Null<Int>>(5));
		rt("Box<Pt>", new Box<Pt>(new Pt()));
		rt("Sub", new Sub());
		rt("Pair", new Pair<Int, String>(1, "x"));
		rt("Array class", Array);
		rt("Box class", Box);
		rt("StringMap class", haxe.ds.StringMap);
		rt("List<Int>", { var l = new List<Int>(); l.add(1); l; });
		rt("StringMap<Int>", ["a" => 1]);
		rt("IntMap<String>", [1 => "a"]);
		rt("Holder", new Holder());
		rt("E.A", A([1, 2]));
		rt("E.B", B(["k" => 1]));
		rt("E.C", C(Some(3)));
		rt("E.C none", C(None));
		rt("E.D", D(new Box(4)));
		rt("E.N", N);
		rt("Option", haxe.ds.Option.Some(1));
		var h:Dynamic = haxe.Unserializer.run(haxe.Serializer.run(new Holder()));
		t("holder.ai", () -> Std.string(Type.getClass(h.ai)) + " " + h.ai);
	}
}

# Casts notes §6.8. The round trip sets the map's existing key instead of a second one ("c"), because a
# two-key StringMap serializes in String.GetHashCode order, randomized per process.
--- cast-unserialize-typed @gencs
// Unserializing a class whose fields are typed instantiations: Unserializer builds X<object> and
// __hx_setField casts into the field (copying, converting with genericCast). Type.createEmptyInstance of a
// generic class, and Type.resolveClass of one. @gencs.
// The round trip overwrites the map's one key (u.m.set("a", 3)): a second key would serialize in
// String.GetHashCode order, which .NET randomizes per process.
class Box<T> {
	public var v:T;
	public var arr:Array<T>;

	public function new(v:T) {
		this.v = v;
		arr = [v];
	}
}

class Typed {
	public var a:Array<Int>;
	public var f:Array<Float>;
	public var m:Map<String, Int>;
	public var l:List<String>;
	public var b:Box<Int>;

	public function new() {}
}

class P {
	static function run(name:String, f:Void->Dynamic) {
		try {
			Sys.println(name + ": " + Std.string(f()));
		} catch (e:Dynamic) {
			var s = Std.string(e);
			if (s.length > 100) s = s.substr(0, 100);
			Sys.println(name + ": EXC " + s.split("\n")[0].split("\r")[0]);
		}
	}

	static function main() {
		run("round trip", () -> {
			var h = new Typed();
			h.a = [1, 2];
			h.f = [1.5];
			h.m = ["a" => 1];
			h.l = new List();
			h.l.add("x");
			h.b = new Box(2);
			var u:Typed = haxe.Unserializer.run(haxe.Serializer.run(h));
			u.m.set("a", 3);
			u.l.add("y");
			u.a.push(3);
			Std.string(Type.typeof(u.a)) + " " + Std.string(Type.typeof(u.m)) + " " + Std.string(Type.typeof(u.l)) + " " + Std.string(Type.typeof(u.b)) + " " + Std.string(Type.typeof(u.b.arr)) + " | " + haxe.Serializer.run(u);
		});
		run("int field from 1.5", () -> { var u:Typed = haxe.Unserializer.run("cy5:Typedy1:aai1d1.5nhg"); haxe.Serializer.run(u); });
		run("float field from null", () -> { var u:Typed = haxe.Unserializer.run("cy5:Typedy1:fai1d1.5nhg"); haxe.Serializer.run(u); });
		run("map field from 1.5", () -> { var u:Typed = haxe.Unserializer.run("cy5:Typedy1:mby1:ad1.5hg"); haxe.Serializer.run(u); });
		run("list field from int", () -> { var u:Typed = haxe.Unserializer.run("cy5:Typedy1:lli1hg"); haxe.Serializer.run(u); });
		run("box field", () -> { var u:Typed = haxe.Unserializer.run("cy5:Typedy1:bcy3:Boxy1:vd2.5y3:arrad2.5hgg"); Std.string(u.b.v) + " " + Std.string(u.b.arr) + " " + Std.string(Type.typeof(u.b)); });
		run("createEmptyInstance", () -> { var b:Box<Int> = Type.createEmptyInstance(Box); b.v = 1; Std.string(Type.typeof(b)); });
		run("createEmptyInstance Dynamic", () -> { var b:Dynamic = Type.createEmptyInstance(Type.resolveClass("Box")); Std.string(Type.typeof(b)); });
		run("resolveClass", () -> Type.getClassName(Type.resolveClass("Box")) + " " + Type.getClassName(Type.resolveClass("haxe.ds.StringMap")));
	}
}
