# Several event shapes together: two event classes and a third in one module (their EventMap rows are grouped
# per type), a subclass calling an inherited accessor, a Haxe interface implemented by a custom and a field-like
# event, a generic delegate type for both kinds, a protected field-like event, closures of add_X (instance and
# static) and GetEvents on each type.
--- event-shapes @gencs
import cs.system.EventHandler;
import cs.system.EventHandler_1;
import cs.system.EventArgs;

interface IPing {
	@:event private var Ping:EventHandler;
	function add_Ping(h:EventHandler):Void;
	function remove_Ping(h:EventHandler):Void;
}

class Base implements IPing {
	public function new() {}
	@:event var Ping:EventHandler;
	var pings:EventHandler;
	public function add_Ping(h:EventHandler):Void {
		Sys.println("Base.add_Ping");
		pings = pings + h;
	}
	public function remove_Ping(h:EventHandler):Void pings = pings - h;
	@:event var Gen:EventHandler_1<EventArgs>;
	var gens:EventHandler_1<EventArgs>;
	public function add_Gen(h:EventHandler_1<EventArgs>):Void gens = gens + h;
	public function remove_Gen(h:EventHandler_1<EventArgs>):Void gens = gens - h;
	public function firePing() if (pings != null) pings.Invoke("base", EventArgs.Empty);
	public function fireGen() if (gens != null) gens.Invoke("base", EventArgs.Empty);
}

class Sub extends Base {
	public function new() super();
	@:event var Auto:EventHandler;
	public function add_Auto(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public function remove_Auto(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	@:event var AutoGen:EventHandler_1<EventArgs>;
	public function add_AutoGen(h:EventHandler_1<EventArgs>):Void {}
	public function remove_AutoGen(h:EventHandler_1<EventArgs>):Void {}
	@:protected @:event var Hidden:EventHandler;
	public function add_Hidden(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public function remove_Hidden(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public function watch() {
		add_Ping(new EventHandler((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("sub watched " + o)));
		add_Gen(new EventHandler_1<EventArgs>((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("sub generic " + o)));
		add_Auto(new EventHandler((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("auto " + o)));
		add_AutoGen(new EventHandler_1<EventArgs>((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("auto generic " + o)));
		add_Hidden(new EventHandler((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("hidden " + o)));
	}
	public function fireAuto() {
		if (Auto != null) Auto.Invoke("sub", EventArgs.Empty);
		if (AutoGen != null) AutoGen.Invoke("sub", EventArgs.Empty);
		if (Hidden != null) Hidden.Invoke("sub", EventArgs.Empty);
	}
}

class Quiet implements IPing {
	public function new() {}
	@:event var Ping:EventHandler;
	public function add_Ping(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public function remove_Ping(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	@:event static var Shared:EventHandler;
	public static function add_Shared(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public static function remove_Shared(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public function raise() if (Ping != null) Ping.Invoke("quiet", EventArgs.Empty);
	public static function raiseShared() if (Shared != null) Shared.Invoke("shared", EventArgs.Empty);
}

class P {
	static function names(t:cs.system.Type) {
		var f = new cs.Flags(cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Public) | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Instance
			| cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Static | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly;
		var evs = t.GetEvents(f);
		return t.Name + " [" + [for (i in 0...evs.Length) evs[i].Name + ":" + evs[i].GetAddMethod(true).Attributes].join("; ") + "]";
	}
	static function main() {
		var s = new Sub();
		s.watch();
		s.firePing();
		s.fireGen();
		s.fireAuto();
		var i:IPing = s;
		i.add_Ping(new EventHandler((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("via interface " + o)));
		s.firePing();
		var q = new Quiet();
		var qi:IPing = q;
		var add = qi.add_Ping;
		add(new EventHandler((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("closure " + o)));
		q.raise();
		var sadd = Quiet.add_Shared;
		sadd(new EventHandler((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("static closure " + o)));
		Quiet.raiseShared();
		Reflect.callMethod(q, Reflect.field(q, "add_Ping"), [new EventHandler((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("reflected " + o))]);
		q.raise();
		Sys.println(names(cs.Lib.toNativeType(IPing)));
		Sys.println(names(cs.Lib.toNativeType(Base)));
		Sys.println(names(cs.Lib.toNativeType(Sub)));
		Sys.println(names(cs.Lib.toNativeType(Quiet)));
	}
}

# -D dotnet-nullable's rows for events, against Roslyn's: the [dump] is the row dump of gencs's C# with the server app's
# `#nullable enable` patch applied by hand (as for attrs-nullable-rows), in hxc's type spellings. An event has the
# Nullable attribute of its type where its type's context is not that byte (Tied: 0), and does not count in the
# context's tally, which has the field-like event's backing field and the accessors' parameters; the CompilerGenerated
# rows of a field-like event's field and accessors, and of an interface's accessors, come after the Nullable ones.
--- attrs-nullable-events @lib @module=tools.P @dump=attrs:tools.Ev,attrs:tools.Tied,attrs:tools.IEv,attrs:tools.Impl + -D dotnet-nullable=tools
package tools;

import cs.system.EventHandler;
import cs.system.EventHandler_1;
import cs.system.EventArgs;

// Most members are 1, so the type's context is 1 and its events carry no attribute of their own.
@:nativeGen class Ev {
	public function new() {}
	@:event var Custom:EventHandler;
	var h:EventHandler;
	public function add_Custom(x:EventHandler):Void h = h + x;
	public function remove_Custom(x:EventHandler):Void h = h - x;
	@:event var Auto:EventHandler_1<EventArgs>;
	public function add_Auto(x:EventHandler_1<EventArgs>):Void {}
	public function remove_Auto(x:EventHandler_1<EventArgs>):Void {}
	@:event static var SAuto:EventHandler;
	public static function add_SAuto(x:EventHandler):Void {}
	public static function remove_SAuto(x:EventHandler):Void {}
}

// Eleven boxed ints and the base type are 0, against the events' accessors and bodies and two fields: the context
// is 0, so the events, the fields and the accessors say 1 themselves.

# A @:event(...) var with (default, set) access is no event (Haxe's check matches only (default, default) vars): it
# compiles as the plain property it is, as haxeui's builder macro makes its @:event vars. gencs still hides it from
# reflection, as it does every @:event var.
--- event-haxeui-builder-vars-are-not-events @gencs
class Btn {
	public function new() {}
	@:event(1) public var onClick(default, set):Void->Void;
	function set_onClick(v:Void->Void):Void->Void {
		Sys.println("set_onClick");
		return onClick = v;
	}
	public function click() if (onClick != null) onClick() else Sys.println("no handler");
}

class P {
	static function main() {
		var b = new Btn();
		b.click();
		b.onClick = () -> Sys.println("clicked");
		b.click();
		Sys.println(cs.Lib.toNativeType(Btn).GetEvent("onClick") == null);
		Sys.println(Reflect.fields(b));
		Sys.println(Type.getInstanceFields(Btn).filter(f -> f.indexOf("onClick") >= 0));
	}
}

# Empty add_/remove_ bodies: gencs writes a field-like C# event, whose private backing field the class reads
# and writes as the var, and whose compiler-generated accessors combine into it with Interlocked.CompareExchange.
--- event-field-like @gencs
import cs.system.EventHandler;
import cs.system.EventArgs;

// Empty add_/remove_ bodies: gencs writes a field-like C# event (`public event EventHandler Changed;`), whose
// compiler-generated accessors combine into a private backing field that the class reads as `Changed`.
class Auto {
	public function new() {}
	@:event var Changed:EventHandler;
	public function add_Changed(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public function remove_Changed(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public function fire(tag:String) {
		if (Changed != null) Changed.Invoke(tag, EventArgs.Empty) else Sys.println("nobody for " + tag);
	}
	public function clear() Changed = null;

	@:event static var SChanged:EventHandler;
	public static function add_SChanged(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public static function remove_SChanged(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public static function sfire(tag:String) {
		if (SChanged != null) SChanged.Invoke(tag, EventArgs.Empty) else Sys.println("nobody for " + tag);
	}
}

class P {
	static function main() {
		var a = new Auto();
		a.fire("a");
		var h1 = new EventHandler((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("one got " + o));
		var h2 = new EventHandler((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("two got " + o));
		a.add_Changed(h1);
		a.add_Changed(h2);
		a.fire("b");
		a.remove_Changed(h1);
		a.fire("c");
		a.clear();
		a.fire("d");
		Auto.add_SChanged(h1);
		Auto.sfire("e");
		var t = cs.Lib.toNativeType(Auto);
		t.GetEvent("Changed").AddEventHandler(a, (cast h2 : cs.system.Delegate));
		a.fire("f");
		var e = t.GetEvent("Changed");
		Sys.println("add " + e.GetAddMethod().Attributes);
		var f = t.GetField("Changed", new cs.Flags(cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic) | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Instance);
		Sys.println("backing " + f.Name + " " + f.Attributes);
		Sys.println(Reflect.fields(a));
	}
}

# A Haxe interface's @:event var: the interface declares the event, its accessors are the interface's add_/remove_
# (abstract, SpecialName, CompilerGenerated), and the class's accessors implement them (virtual final newslot).
--- event-haxe-interface @gencs
import cs.system.EventHandler;
import cs.system.EventArgs;

// A Haxe interface's @:event var is a C# interface event, whose accessors are the interface's add_/remove_.
interface INotify {
	@:event private var Changed:EventHandler;
	function add_Changed(h:EventHandler):Void;
	function remove_Changed(h:EventHandler):Void;
}

class Impl implements INotify {
	public function new() {}
	@:event var Changed:EventHandler;
	var handlers:EventHandler;
	public function add_Changed(h:EventHandler):Void {
		Sys.println("Impl.add_Changed");
		handlers = handlers + h;
	}
	public function remove_Changed(h:EventHandler):Void {
		handlers = handlers - h;
	}
	public function fire(tag:String) if (handlers != null) handlers.Invoke(tag, EventArgs.Empty);
}

class P {
	static function main() {
		var i:INotify = new Impl();
		var h = new EventHandler((o:Dynamic, e:EventArgs) -> Sys.println("got " + o));
		i.add_Changed(h);
		(cast i : Impl).fire("a");
		i.remove_Changed(h);
		(cast i : Impl).fire("b");
		for (t in [cs.Lib.toNativeType(INotify), cs.Lib.toNativeType(Impl)]) {
			var e = t.GetEvent("Changed");
			Sys.println(t.Name + " " + e.Name + " add=" + e.GetAddMethod().Attributes);
		}
		// C#'s `((INotify)x).Changed += h`, through the interface's EventInfo.
		cs.Lib.toNativeType(INotify).GetEvent("Changed").AddEventHandler(i, (cast h : cs.system.Delegate));
		(cast i : Impl).fire("c");
	}
}

# Overriding a .NET event's accessors with @:overload override: gencs writes C# methods (CS0115, and CS0534 for the
# abstract event), while the CLR overrides add_Virt by name and signature, which hxc already does.
# Kept as is: the base class's Event row describes the event.
--- netlib-event-accessor-override @netlib=EvLib
import ev.*;
class Der extends Base {
  public function new() super();
  var a:Note;
  @:overload override public function add_Virt(n:Note):Void { Sys.println("Der.add_Virt"); super.add_Virt(n); }
  @:overload override public function remove_Virt(n:Note):Void { super.remove_Virt(n); }
  @:overload public function add_Abs(n:Note):Void { Sys.println("Der.add_Abs"); a = a + n; }
  @:overload public function remove_Abs(n:Note):Void { a = a - n; }
  public function fireAbs(s:String) if (a != null) a.Invoke(s);
}
class P {
  static function main() {
    var d = new Der();
    Use.SubscribeVirt(d, "cs");
    d.FireVirt("v");
    Use.SubscribeAbs(d, "cs");
    d.fireAbs("x");
  }
}

# A Haxe class implementing a .NET interface's event: C# subscribes with += through the interface
# (callvirt INotify::add_Noted) and through EventInfo.AddEventHandler.
--- netlib-event-implements-interface @gencs @netlib=EvLib
import ev.*;
class Src implements INotify {
  public function new() {}
  @:event var Noted:Note;
  var h:Note;
  public function add_Noted(n:Note):Void { Sys.println("Src.add_Noted"); h = h + n; }
  public function remove_Noted(n:Note):Void { Sys.println("Src.remove_Noted"); h = h - n; }
  public function fire(s:String) { if (h != null) h.Invoke(s); else Sys.println("nobody for " + s); }
}
class Plain {
  public function new() {}
  @:event var Changed:Note;
  var h:Note;
  public function add_Changed(n:Note):Void { h = h + n; }
  public function remove_Changed(n:Note):Void { h = h - n; }
  public function fire(s:String) { if (h != null) h.Invoke(s); else Sys.println("nobody for " + s); }
  @:event static var SChanged:Note;
  static var sh:Note;
  public static function add_SChanged(n:Note):Void { sh = sh + n; }
  public static function remove_SChanged(n:Note):Void { sh = sh - n; }
  public static function sfire(s:String) { if (sh != null) sh.Invoke(s); else Sys.println("nobody for " + s); }
}
class P {
  static function main() {
    var s = new Src();
    Use.Subscribe(s, "cs");
    s.fire("a");
    var i:INotify = s;
    var d = new Note((x) -> Sys.println("haxe got " + x));
    i.add_Noted(d);
    s.fire("b");
    i.remove_Noted(d);
    s.fire("c");
    Sys.println(Use.Events(cs.Lib.toNativeType(Src)));
    Sys.println(Use.Reflect(s, "Noted"));
    s.fire("d");
    var p = new Plain();
    Sys.println(Use.Events(cs.Lib.toNativeType(Plain)));
    Sys.println(Use.Reflect(p, "Changed"));
    p.fire("e");
    Sys.println(Use.Reflect(cs.Lib.toNativeType(Plain), "SChanged"));
    Plain.sfire("f");
    p.add_Changed(d);
    p.fire("g");
    Reflect.callMethod(p, Reflect.field(p, "remove_Changed"), [d]);
    p.fire("h");
    Sys.println(Type.getInstanceFields(Plain).filter(f -> f.indexOf("Changed") >= 0));
    Sys.println(Type.getClassFields(Plain).filter(f -> f.indexOf("Changed") >= 0));
  }
}

# gencs's RenameTypeParameters: per class, a counter starting at 0 and the set of names in use (the class's type
# parameters, then each field's own); a method type parameter whose name is taken becomes name + the next
# counter value not taken, over the instance fields first, then the statics. Only GenericParam names show it.
--- method-type-param-renamed @gencs
class G<T> {
	public function new() {}
	public static function s<T>(x:T):T return x;
	public function i<T>(x:T):T return x;
	public function j<U>(x:U):U return x;
}
class K<T> extends G<T> {
	public function new() super();
	public function k<T>(x:T):T return x;
}
class L<T> {
	public function new() {}
	public static function s<T1, T>(a:T1, x:T):T return x;
}
class M {
	public static function s<T>(x:T):T return x;
}
class P {
	static function show(c:Class<Dynamic>) {
		var t = cs.Lib.toNativeType(c);
		var out = [];
		for (m in t.GetMethods()) if (m.IsGenericMethodDefinition && m.DeclaringType == t) {
			var ps = [for (a in m.GetGenericArguments()) a.Name];
			out.push(m.Name + "<" + ps.join(",") + ">");
		}
		out.sort(Reflect.compare);
		Sys.println(t.Name + " " + out.join(" "));
	}
	static function main() {
		show(G); show(K); show(L); show(M);
		Sys.println(G.s(1) + new G<String>().i(2) + new K<Int>().k(4) + L.s(1, 2) + M.s(3));
	}
}

# Divergence from gencs, whose C# for these fails with CS0246: it renames a method type parameter and keeps the
# renamed name in the signature of an override of a renamed generic method (`K<T> extends G<T>`, `override
# i<T>(x:T)` is `T1 i<T2>(T1 x)`), and for `H<T, T1>.s<T>` it declares one name and uses another. hxc renames by
# the same rule and uses the new name in the whole signature, so both compile and run.
--- method-type-param-renamed-override
class G<T> {
	public function new() {}
	public function i<T>(x:T):T return x;
}
class K<T> extends G<T> {
	public function new() super();
	override public function i<T>(x:T):T return x;
	public function k<T>(x:T):T return x;
}
class H<T, T1> {
	public function new() {}
	public static function s<T>(x:T):T return x;
}
class P {
	static function show(c:Class<Dynamic>) {
		var t = cs.Lib.toNativeType(c);
		var out = [];
		for (m in t.GetMethods()) if (m.IsGenericMethodDefinition && m.DeclaringType == t) {
			var ps = [for (a in m.GetGenericArguments()) a.Name];
			out.push(m.Name + "<" + ps.join(",") + ">");
		}
		out.sort(Reflect.compare);
		Sys.println(t.Name + " " + out.join(" "));
	}
	static function main() {
		show(G); show(K); show(H);
		var g:G<Int> = new K<Int>();
		Sys.println(g.i(5) + " " + new K<String>().i("a") + " " + new K<Int>().k(7) + " " + H.s(9));
	}
}

# The rename covers an interface's methods (the companion's too: m mentions no class type parameter), a
# constructor's own type parameter and an @:overload method's overloads, by the same counter.
--- method-type-param-renamed-members @gencs
interface I<T> {
	function m<T>(x:T):T;
	function n<T>(x:T, y:T):T;
}
class C<T> implements I<T> {
	public function new() {}
	public function m<T>(x:T):T return x;
	public function n<T>(x:T, y:T):T return y;
	@:overload public function o<T>(x:T):T return x;
	@:overload public function o<T>(x:T, y:Int):T return x;

}
interface J {
	function q<T>(x:T):T;
}
class P {
	static function show(c:Class<Dynamic>) {
		var t = cs.Lib.toNativeType(c);
		var out = [];
		for (m in t.GetMethods()) if (m.IsGenericMethodDefinition && m.DeclaringType == t) {
			var ps = [for (a in m.GetGenericArguments()) a.Name];
			out.push(m.Name + "<" + ps.join(",") + ">");
		}
		out.sort(Reflect.compare);
		Sys.println(t.Name + " " + out.join(" "));
	}
	static function main() {
		show(I); show(C); show(J);
		var i:I<String> = new C<String>();
		var c = new C<Int>();
		Sys.println(i.m(1) + " " + i.n(1, 2) + " " + c.o(3) + " " + c.o(4, 5) + " " + c.p(6));
	}

# An interface a subclass lists, implemented by a final or inline method of its Haxe superclass. Roslyn makes
# such a method of the same compilation `virtual final newslot` (B.m implements I in B already; B.n and the inline
# B.k implement J and K only for D) and adds no stub, so a call through the interface reaches it. Replaces

# The same two levels up, and what C# and reflection see of it: the method B.n a subclass of a subclass lists an
# interface for is `virtual final` (IsVirtual and IsFinal, the slot of the interface method), as is the inline
# one; a final method nothing lists stays non-virtual, and a call by the class (D.n, E.n) still reaches B's. The
# interface method of a generic interface is bound through the base's type arguments.
--- iface-method-inherited-final-two-levels-and-reflection @gencs
interface J { function n():Int; }
interface G<T> { function g(x:T):T; }
class B {
	public function new() {}
	public final function n():Int return 2;
	public inline function k():Int return 3;
	public final function g(x:Int):Int return x + 1;
	public final function plain():Int return 4;
}
class D extends B {
	public function new() super();
}
class E extends D implements J implements G<Int> {
	public function new() super();
}
interface K { function k():Int; }
class F extends E implements K {
	public function new() super();
}
class P {
	static function main() {
		var e = new E();
		var j:J = e, g:G<Int> = e, k:K = new F();
		Sys.println(j.n() + " " + g.g(5) + " " + k.k() + " " + e.n() + " " + e.plain());
		var t = cs.Lib.toNativeType(B);
		for (n in ["n", "k", "g", "plain"]) {
			var m = t.GetMethod(n);
			Sys.println(n + " virtual=" + m.IsVirtual + " final=" + m.IsFinal);
		}
	}
}

# Overriding what a subclass's interface maps to: Haxe refuses an override of an inline or final method, so the base's
# method, now `virtual final newslot` for an interface of a subclass, is never overridden (a CLR override of a sealed

	public function new() super();
	public function k():Int return 6;

# A method group over a final method that an interface of a subclass maps to (it is `virtual final` now), and over one
# nothing maps. On a null receiver the creation throws System.ArgumentException in gencs's build and in hxc's, for the
# mapped method and the plain one alike, and a live receiver's delegate runs the method, so making the first
# `virtual final` changed nothing a program can see here.
--- delegate-method-group-inherited-final-null-receiver @gencs + -D net-ver=40
import cs.system.Func_1;
interface J { function n():Int; }
class B {
	public function new() {}
	public final function n():Int return 2;
	public final function plain():Int return 3;
}
class D extends B implements J { public function new() super(); }
class P {
	static function viaN(d:D):Func_1<Int> return d.n;
	static function viaPlain(d:D):Func_1<Int> return d.plain;
	static function show(tag:String, make:() -> Func_1<Int>) {
		var f = null;
		try {
			f = make();
			Sys.println(tag + " made");
		} catch (e:Dynamic) {
			Sys.println(tag + " threw " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e)));
			return;
		}
		try {
			Sys.println(tag + " " + f.Invoke());
		} catch (e:Dynamic) {
			Sys.println(tag + " invoke threw " + Type.getClassName(Type.getClass(e)));
		}
	}
	static function main() {
		show("n live", () -> viaN(new D()));
		show("n null", () -> viaN(null));
		show("plain live", () -> viaPlain(new D()));
		show("plain null", () -> viaPlain(null));
	}
}

# gencs's method order, seen through .NET reflection: the static members (sm) come right after the constructors,

# The order for a class with every member kind, as gencs writes it (MethodDef order, which GetMethods follows): the
# entry point, the static constructor and the constructors, the static events' accessors, __hx_ctor_*, the statics
# in declaration order (a generic class's static __hx_cast first), then the instance events' accessors, the
# properties' accessors, the cast and the other instance methods, and last the reflection members and ToString.
# An interface keeps its own order, a struct writes its static method before the instance one. A static
# @:property var's accessors (get_sip, set_sip) are among the statics in declaration order, not ahead of
# __hx_ctor_*: gencs dumps with the var declared before and after a static method both give that. The accessors of a
# static property with get/set methods do come before __hx_ctor_*, but hxc refuses those. G is a generic class with
# a static event.
--- member-order-every-member-kind @gencs
import cs.system.EventHandler;
import cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags;

class C {
	public var a:Int = 1;
	public static var s1 = 2;
	@:property public var ip:Int = 3;
	@:property public static var sip:Int = 4;
	@:property public var pa(get, set):Int;
	function get_pa() return a;
	function set_pa(v) return a = v;
	@:event var Ev:EventHandler;
	public function add_Ev(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public function remove_Ev(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	@:event static var SEv:EventHandler;
	public static function add_SEv(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public static function remove_SEv(h:EventHandler):Void {}

# What still differs from gencs's member order, all in the members of an @:event var and in the Field table (spec,
# Interop divergences). hxc's output is the expectation; gencs's real net10.0 run printed:
#   E methods: add_SEv,remove_SEv,__hx_ctor__E,sa,_remove_SEv,_add_SEv,add_Ev2,remove_Ev2,add_Ev,remove_Ev,m1,toString,__hx_setField,__hx_getField,__hx_invokeField,__hx_getFields,_remove_Ev2,_add_Ev2,_remove_Ev,_add_Ev,ToString
#   E fields by token: sh,h
#   F fields by token: SEv,s1,s2,Ev,a,b
#   G`1 fields by token: __hx_init_called,SEv,sv,t
# (every other line below is the same in gencs's run). A custom event's private _add_X/_remove_X: gencs writes a
# static event's after the statics and an instance event's after the reflection members, before ToString, each
# event's pair as _remove_X then _add_X and the events in reverse declaration order; hxc leaves them at their
# declaration position, _add_X then _remove_X. A field-like event's backing field: gencs puts it first among the
# instance fields (or the static fields), hxc in declaration order. The Field table: gencs lists the static
# fields first, hxc the instance fields (GetFields is unaffected, the CLR lists instance fields first; the
# MetadataToken order shows it), and gencs puts a generic class's __hx_init_called first, hxc last.
--- member-order-event-members-and-fields-differ-from-gencs
import cs.system.EventHandler;
import cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags;

class E {
	public static function sa() {}
	var h:EventHandler;
	@:event var Ev:EventHandler;
	public function add_Ev(h2:EventHandler):Void { h = h + h2; }
	public function remove_Ev(h2:EventHandler):Void { h = h - h2; }
	@:event static var SEv:EventHandler;
	static var sh:EventHandler;
	public static function add_SEv(h2:EventHandler):Void { sh = sh + h2; }
	public static function remove_SEv(h2:EventHandler):Void { sh = sh - h2; }
	public function new() {}
	public function m1() {}
	@:event var Ev2:EventHandler;
	public function add_Ev2(h2:EventHandler):Void { h = h + h2; }
	public function remove_Ev2(h2:EventHandler):Void { h = h - h2; }
	public function toString() return "E";
}

class F {
	public var a:Int = 1;
	public static var s1 = 2;
	@:event var Ev:EventHandler;
	public function add_Ev(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public function remove_Ev(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	@:event static var SEv:EventHandler;
	public static function add_SEv(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public static function remove_SEv(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public var b:Int = 3;
	public static var s2 = 4;
	public function new() {}
}

class G<T> {
	public var t:T;
	public static var sv = 4;
	@:event static var SEv:EventHandler;
	public static function add_SEv(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public static function remove_SEv(h:EventHandler):Void {}
	public static function st() return 1;
	public function new() {}
	public function m1(x:T) return x;
}

class P {
	static function main() {
		new E();
		new F();
		new G<Int>().m1(1);
		G.st();

		for (t in [cs.Lib.toNativeType(E), cs.Lib.toNativeType(F), cs.Lib.toNativeType(G)]) {
			var ms = t.GetMethods(all);
			Sys.println(t.Name + " methods: " + [for (i in 0...ms.Length) ms[i].Name].join(","));
			var fs = t.GetFields(all);
			var l = [for (i in 0...fs.Length) fs[i]];
			l.sort((x, y) -> x.MetadataToken - y.MetadataToken);
			Sys.println(t.Name + " fields by token: " + [for (f in l) f.Name].join(","));
			var es = t.GetEvents(all);

class Item {
	public var id:Int = 0;
	public function new() {}

	static function read<T>(r:() -> T):T return r();

# gencs writes the optional-argument overloads of an abstract's implementation class too, as it does for a
# @:nativeGen class (the server app's Guid abstract: `_new()` beside `_new(guidstr)`). Not for a class in its class
# model (Plain), and each has the field's attributes (EditorBrowsable for a @:noCompletion method).
--- optional-overloads-of-abstract-implementation-class @gencs
abstract A(String) {
	@:noCompletion
	function new(s:String = null) this = s;

	public static function make():A return new A();

	public static function viaDefault(?k:Int, ?j:Int):Null<Int> return k;

	public function inst(?z:Int):Null<Int> return z;
}

class Plain {
	public static function f(?a:String) return a;
}

class P {
	static function describe(t:cs.system.Type) {
		var all = new cs.Flags(cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Public) | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic
			| cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Static | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.Instance | cs.system.reflection.BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly;
		var ms = t.GetMethods(all);
		var l = [for (i in 0...ms.Length) ms[i]];
		l.sort((x, y) -> Reflect.compare(x.MetadataToken, y.MetadataToken));
		var out = [];
		for (m in l) {
			var attrs = m.GetCustomAttributes(cs.Lib.toNativeType(cs.system.componentmodel.EditorBrowsableAttribute), false);
			out.push(m.Name + "/" + m.GetParameters().Length + (attrs.Length > 0 ? "*" : ""));
		}
		return out.join(" ");
	}

	static function main() {
		Sys.println(describe(cs.system.Type.GetType("_P.A_Impl_")));
		Sys.println(describe(cs.Lib.toNativeType(Plain)));
		Sys.println(A.make() == null);
	}
}

# gencs's C#: P.cs(8,13): error CS0079: The event 'A.SChanged' can only appear on the left hand side of += or -=
# (from `static A() { global::A.SChanged = global::A.mk(); }`).
--- event-static-initializer-is-an-error
import cs.system.EventHandler;

// A custom event has no value, so no initializer either: gencs writes the initializer as an assignment in the static
// constructor, next to `public static event EventHandler SChanged { add {...} remove {...} }`, which is CS0079. hxc
// once dropped the initializer (and its side effects) without a word.
class A {
	static var handlers:EventHandler;
	static function mk():EventHandler { Sys.println("initializer ran"); return null; }
	@:event static var SChanged:EventHandler = mk();
	public static function add_SChanged(h:EventHandler):Void { Sys.println("add body"); handlers = handlers + h; }
	public static function remove_SChanged(h:EventHandler):Void handlers = handlers - h;
}

class P {
	static function main() {
		A.add_SChanged(null);
	}
}

@:native("System.Reflection.CustomAttributeData") extern class AttrData {
	static function GetCustomAttributes(t:cs.system.Type):cs.system.collections.IEnumerable;

@:meta(System.Obsolete("old"))
@:meta(System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComVisible(false))
class Grid implements ArrayAccess<Int> {
	var cells = [10, 20, 30];
	public function new() {}
	public function __get(i:Int):Int return cells[i];
	public function __set(i:Int, v:Int):Int return cells[i] = v;
